items.summary: Adriano Galliani, a candidate for president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), has decided not to challenge the admission of Giovanni Malagò's candidacy ahead of the election on 14 December.
items.imageAlt: Adriano Galliani, file photo

items.title: Romelu Lukaku retires from Belgium duty after 94 goals in 135 games
items.summary: Striker Romelu Lukaku, the all-time leading scorer of Belgium's men's team, announced on Monday, 16 November, that he has retired from international football after 16 years.
items.imageAlt: Romelu Lukaku playing for Belgium against the United States at the 2026 World Cup

items.title: Five European countries expected to announce a migrant return centre in Kigali
items.summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to announce that a centre for asylum seekers refused the right to stay in the European Union will be built in Rwanda's capital, Kigali, diplomatic sources told the BBC.
items.imageAlt: A view of Kigali, the capital of Rwanda

items.title: Puntland finance minister tells parliament civil servants have gone 6 months without pay
items.summary: Puntland's Finance Minister, Mohamed Farah Mohamud, admitted before parliament on Monday, 16 November, that the state's civil servants have not been paid for 6 months, as he also submitted the 2027 budget to lawmakers.
items.imageAlt: An overview of Garowe, the capital of Puntland

items.title: Drake Maye suffers serious ankle injury, Patriots may lose him for the rest of the season
items.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered a serious ankle injury in the Patriots' defeat to the Detroit Lions in Munich and is expected to be out for an extended period, possibly the rest of the season.
items.imageAlt: Gillette Stadium, home of the New England Patriots (file photo, 2021)

items.title: Dino Sani, 1958 World Cup winner with Brazil and former AC Milan player, dies aged 94
items.summary: Dino Sani, the former Brazil and AC Milan midfielder, died in São Paulo on Sunday, 15 November, aged 94, the Brazilian Football Confederation confirmed.
items.imageAlt: Dino Sani in 2008

items.title: US sends a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East as Iran says it remains committed to diplomacy
items.summary: The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the Middle East on Monday, 16 November, while Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in Islamabad that his country remains committed to diplomacy.
items.imageAlt: The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt at sea (file photo)

items.title: Hargeisa court jails politician who said he would run for Somalia's presidency and the journalist who interviewed him
items.summary: The Maroodi-jeex regional court in Hargeisa on Monday, 16 November, sentenced politician Abdiqadir Mohamed Sharaay and journalist Abdirahman Ige to prison, after an interview in which Sharaay spoke of his ambition to run for President of Somalia.
items.imageAlt: A street market in the city of Hargeisa

items.title: Nike to replace Adidas as Champions League ball supplier from 2027
items.summary: US company Nike will become the official ball supplier for UEFA's men's club competitions from the 2027/28 season, replacing Adidas, which has provided the Champions League ball since 2001.
items.imageAlt: UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland (file photo)

items.title: China: Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss world peace in Shenzhen
items.summary: China's Foreign Ministry confirmed on Monday that President Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will hold their first trilateral summit in the city of Shenzhen on Thursday, 19 November, where they will discuss world peace and strategic stability.
items.imageAlt: Presidents Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping meeting in Beijing (2025)

items.title: Custodial Corps foils attempt to smuggle drugs into Mogadishu Central Prison
items.summary: The command of the Somali Custodial Corps said on Monday that it had seized drugs that were to be smuggled into Mogadishu Central Prison, and six women were arrested after an operation lasting two months.
items.imageAlt: Prison guards at Mogadishu Central Prison (2013)

items.title: US to renew support for the UNSOS office and the AUSSOM mission
items.summary: The US State Department has confirmed to the AFP news agency that Washington will support a one-year extension of the mandate of the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) and the African Union mission AUSSOM.
items.imageAlt: A ceremony in Mogadishu bidding farewell to former UNSOS head Lisa Filipetto (2023)

items.title: World Bank weighing suspension of budget support to Somalia
items.summary: The World Bank is considering suspending its support for the budget of Somalia's federal government as the dispute over President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension deepens, Hiiraan Online reported on Monday, 16 November.
items.imageAlt: The World Bank Group headquarters in Washington, D.C.

items.title: Russia says it shot down 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight; Crimea bridge attacked
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said on Monday that its air defences shot down 1,336 drones launched by Ukraine overnight, hundreds of them heading for Moscow, while the governor of Crimea said the Crimea bridge had been attacked.
items.imageAlt: The Crimean Bridge at Kerch (2021)

items.title: Special report: The record and leadership of Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre's government
items.summary: A special report on the work of Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre's government: state-building, development, security, diplomacy and good governance.
items.imageAlt: Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre in front of the Somali flag

items.title: Sudan and Ethiopia accuse each other of backing armed groups
items.summary: Tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia have escalated further, with each country accusing the other of backing armed groups fighting inside its borders, the AP news agency reported.
items.imageAlt: Ethiopian army chief Field Marshal Birhanu Jula (2019)

items.title: Kenya opens investigation into looting of refugee offices in Hagadera, Dadaab
items.summary: The Kenyan government has appealed for calm in Hagadera, Dadaab, after offices of the Department of Refugee Services were destroyed and looted, allegedly by a group of young refugees.
items.imageAlt: Refugee shelters in the Dadaab camp, northern Kenya (2011)

items.title: Ugandan AUSSOM troops hand over five bases in Barawe to the Somali National Army
items.summary: Ugandan troops serving with the African Union mission AUSSOM on Monday, 16 November, handed over five bases in the Barawe area of Lower Shabelle region to the Somali National Army.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan troops of the African Union mission in Barawe, Lower Shabelle region (2017)

items.title: Martine Moïse, widow of President Jovenel Moïse, registers as a presidential candidate in Haiti
items.summary: Martine Moïse, the widow of former Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, who was assassinated in 2021, has registered as a presidential candidate for next year's election.
items.imageAlt: Martine Moïse attending a meeting in Haiti, December 2018

items.title: San Antonio Spurs and Wembanyama reach 12 straight wins after beating Utah Jazz 110-102
items.summary: The San Antonio Spurs beat the Utah Jazz 110-102 on Sunday for their 12th consecutive NBA win, with Victor Wembanyama scoring 26 points.
items.imageAlt: Victor Wembanyama playing for the San Antonio Spurs (file photo, 2025)

items.title: 49ers beat Cowboys 46-40, a score never seen before in NFL history
items.summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Dallas Cowboys 46-40 in Dallas on Sunday, 15 November, an 86-point game whose final score had never happened before in the NFL.
items.imageAlt: File photo: AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, home of the Dallas Cowboys

items.title: Toronto Tempo win the WNBA draft lottery and the No. 1 pick in 2027
items.summary: Expansion team Toronto Tempo won the WNBA draft lottery on Sunday, 15 November, securing the No. 1 pick in 2027, which could give them the chance to select USC star JuJu Watkins.
items.imageAlt: File photo: JuJu Watkins, the USC basketball star, at an NFL game in 2025

items.title: US Army officer files complaint against the Pentagon over Iranian strike that killed 6 soldiers in Kuwait
items.summary: A US Army officer who survived an Iranian drone strike on a US post in Kuwait that killed 6 soldiers has filed a complaint with Congress saying military leaders ignored concerns about the post's defences.
items.imageAlt: File photo: the Pentagon, headquarters of the US Department of Defense, seen from the air

items.title: Mirra Andreeva beats Svitolina in the final to win the WTA Finals
items.summary: Russia's Mirra Andreeva, 19, beat Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in the WTA Finals final in Indian Wells on Sunday 15 November, becoming the youngest winner of the event in 22 years.
items.imageAlt: File photo: Mirra Andreeva playing at the 2023 US Open

items.title: Prince Harry makes surprise visit to Lviv, calls wounded veterans role models
items.summary: Britain's Prince Harry on Sunday 15 November wrapped up an unannounced visit to the city of Lviv in western Ukraine, where he praised soldiers wounded in the war and described them as society's role models, the AP news agency reported.
items.imageAlt: File photo: Prince Harry at the opening ceremony of the 2017 Invictus Games

items.title: Bessent urges Nvidia to hire an outside chief, as Musk backs Huang's return
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday 15 November urged Nvidia's board to look outside the company for its new chief executive, as Elon Musk joined more than 158,000 people who have signed a letter demanding that Jensen Huang be reinstated.
items.imageAlt: File photo: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, official portrait from 2025

items.title: Klopp calls for change at the top of FIFA and criticises Infantino
items.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp called on Sunday, 15 November, for a change in the presidency of football's world governing body FIFA, criticising president Gianni Infantino.
items.imageAlt: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's national team coach, pictured in 2019

items.title: EU boards tanker suspected of belonging to Russia's 'shadow fleet'
items.summary: European Union naval forces boarded a tanker named MV MIDAG in the Mediterranean, suspected of belonging to Russia's shadow fleet, and established that it was flying a false flag, the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Sunday, 15 November.
items.imageAlt: Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief

items.title: Africa CDC: Congo's Ebola outbreak still not under control, six months after it was declared
items.summary: The head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), Jean Kaseya, said on Sunday, 15 November, that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is still not under control, warning it could become the worst outbreak the world has seen if it is not stopped now.
items.imageAlt: Jean Kaseya, director-general of Africa CDC, signing a memorandum of understanding in 2025

items.title: Hassan Sheikh: Israel and Taiwan threaten Somalia's existence and statehood
items.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said in Mogadishu on Sunday, 15 November, that Israel and Taiwan pose a threat to Somalia's existence and sovereignty, accusing them of taking steps against the country's unity.
items.imageAlt: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud

items.title: Yemen: Houthis advance to within 60 km of Aden, military sources say
items.summary: Houthi forces in Yemen advanced on Sunday, 15 November, to about 60 kilometres from the city of Aden, the temporary capital of the internationally recognised government, military and government sources told the AFP news agency.
items.imageAlt: The port and buildings in the city of Aden, southern Yemen

items.title: Ronaldinho, 46, plays 45 minutes for Ravenna in his first match since 2015
items.summary: Former Brazil star Ronaldinho returned to the pitch on Sunday, 15 November, aged 46, playing the whole first half for Ravenna in Italy's Serie C in a 2-0 win over local rivals Forlì.
items.imageAlt: Former Brazil star Ronaldinho, pictured in 2016

items.title: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia from 1 December
items.summary: Estonia's Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday, 15 November, that his country will close all border crossings with Russia from 1 December, after an attempted arson attack on a defence company that Tallinn blamed on Moscow.
items.imageAlt: The border between Estonia and Russia on the Narva river, with Ivangorod fortress in the background

items.title: Tens of thousands rally in Prague against plan to change public media funding
items.summary: Tens of thousands of people gathered in Letná Park in Prague, the capital of the Czech Republic, on Sunday, 15 November, to oppose a government plan to change how public service media are funded.
items.imageAlt: A protest placard against Andrej Babiš at a 2019 demonstration in Letná Park in Prague

items.title: Hirshabelle appoints Colonel Abdullahi Barre Ilmi as governor of Hiiraan region
items.summary: Hirshabelle leader Ali Abdullahi Hussein (Gudlawe) on Sunday, 15 November, appointed Colonel Abdullahi Barre Ilmi as the new governor of the Hiiraan region.
items.imageAlt: An African Union soldier on guard in a street in central Beledweyne, capital of the Hiiraan region (2012 photo)

items.title: Ruto urges Ntutu and Tongoyo to rein in supporters after chaos at Maa festival
items.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto on Sunday, 15 November, urged Narok Governor Patrick Ole Ntutu and Narok West MP Gabriel Tongoyo to rein in their supporters after chaotic scenes at the Maa Cultural and Tourism Celebrations on Saturday.
items.imageAlt: A view of Narok town in Kenya

items.title: Yemen's Houthis release 600 conflict-related detainees in Sanaa, ICRC says
items.summary: Yemen's Houthi group has released 600 people detained in connection with the country's conflict in the city of Sanaa under an amnesty it declared unilaterally, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) and Houthi officials said.
items.imageAlt: Buildings in the old city of Sanaa, Yemen

items.title: US loses measles elimination status after a year of outbreaks
items.summary: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has announced that the United States has lost its measles elimination status after a panel of experts found that the virus had spread in the country without interruption for more than 12 months.
items.imageAlt: The MMR vaccine against measles, mumps and rubella

items.title: Iran launches drone attack on US base in Bahrain
items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Sunday, 15 November, that it had targeted a US radar facility at Riffa air base in Bahrain with 6 drones, while Bahrain said its air defences destroyed the attack.
items.imageAlt: The clock tower in the city of Riffa, Bahrain

items.title: Ukrainian drone strikes hit Nizhnekamsk and Taganrog in Russia
items.summary: Russian officials said on Sunday, 15 November, that overnight Ukrainian drone attacks damaged industrial facilities in the city of Nizhnekamsk, while a separate strike on Taganrog killed an engineer working at an electricity substation.
items.imageAlt: The city of Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan covered in snow

items.title: Hassan Sheikh lays foundation stone for National Defence University, urges opposition to return to talks
items.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on Sunday, 15 November, laid the foundation stone for the National Defence University and the reconstruction of the Somali National Army Hospital, and used the occasion to urge opposition politicians to return to the negotiating table.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud during an official visit

items.title: Ruto responds to opposition corruption claims over the SGR railway
items.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto on Sunday, 15 November, accused opposition leaders of selectively quoting a World Bank report that raised concerns about corruption and procurement weaknesses in the construction of the SGR railway, saying the project was carried out under a previous administration.
items.imageAlt: A passenger train on the Mombasa–Nairobi SGR line

items.title: Hamas confirms its Rafah commander, Samir Abu Younis, was killed in an Israeli strike
items.summary: Hamas's military wing, the al-Qassam Brigades, announced on Sunday, 15 November, that its Rafah brigade commander, Samir Abu Younis, was killed in an Israeli strike in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, the Anadolu news agency reported in Daily Sabah.
items.imageAlt: General view of the city of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, 2019

items.title: Prime Minister Hamza: Somalia needs the capacity to defend itself against cyberattacks
items.summary: Somalia's Prime Minister, Hamza Abdi Barre, said on Sunday, 15 November, that Somalia must build the capacity to counter cyberattacks and digital security threats, during a visit to the headquarters of the Ministry of Communications and Technology in Mogadishu.
items.imageAlt: Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre attending a conference in Mogadishu, January 2023

items.title: Australia beat New Zealand 32-12 in the Rugby League World Cup final
items.summary: Australia won the men's Rugby League World Cup for a fourth successive time on Sunday, 15 November, beating New Zealand 32-12 in the final at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane.
items.imageAlt: Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane, Australia

items.title: Senator Ted Cruz urges the US State Department to recognise Somaliland
items.summary: US Senator Ted Cruz has again called for the United States to formally recognise Somaliland, saying in a post on X that the State Department should take steps in line with President Donald Trump's view.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of Senator Ted Cruz, 2019

items.title: Cape Verde votes for president as Neves faces the first woman candidate
items.summary: Voters in Cape Verde are casting ballots in a presidential election on Sunday, 15 November, in which President José Maria Neves is seeking a second term against Joana Rosa, the first woman to run for president in the country.
items.imageAlt: Cape Verde President José Maria Neves, 2023

items.title: Nigeria warns its citizens against transiting Addis Ababa's Bole airport for health reasons
items.summary: Nigeria's foreign ministry has cautioned its citizens, especially those with medical conditions, against travelling via Bole airport in Addis Ababa because of the city's high altitude, after 16 Nigerians died this year while transiting.
items.imageAlt: Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

items.title: Yemen: southern forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb and Dhubab airport as Houthis take over
items.summary: Yemen's Southern Armed Forces have pulled out of Dhubab airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area west of Taiz province, leaving the position to Houthi forces.
items.imageAlt: The Bab el-Mandeb strait seen from mid-channel, with the coast of Yemen visible in the distance

items.title: Jordan: three men sentenced to death over Karak church attack that killed 9
items.summary: Jordan's State Security Court has sentenced three men to death by hanging after finding them guilty of carrying out the armed attack on a church in the south of the country on 23 October, the Jordanian armed forces said.
items.imageAlt: A general view of the town of Al-Karak in southern Jordan

items.title: Ahmed Madobe to travel to Garowe to discuss election dispute with Deni
items.summary: Jubaland President Ahmed Mohamed Islam (Ahmed Madobe) is expected to visit Garowe in the coming days to discuss the dispute over Somalia's electoral process with Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni.
items.imageAlt: Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni at the State House in Garowe, January 2021

items.title: Somalia joins 133 countries backing UN resolution on a moratorium on the death penalty
items.summary: Somalia voted for a resolution adopted by the Third Committee of the United Nations General Assembly on 13 November 2026, calling on states to halt executions.
items.imageAlt: The United Nations General Assembly hall at UN headquarters in New York, 2024

items.title: Moyale: more than 10,000 people displaced inside Kenya amid fears of disease
items.summary: The governor of Kenya's Marsabit County has said more than 10,000 people have been displaced inside Kenya by the conflict in the Moyale area on the Ethiopian border.
items.imageAlt: The highway linking Kenya and Ethiopia, which starts at the Kenyan border at Moyale

items.title: UFC 334: Ciryl Gane beats Josh Hokit by unanimous decision to retain heavyweight title
items.summary: France's Ciryl Gane defended the UFC heavyweight championship after beating Josh Hokit by unanimous decision (48-47, 48-47, 48-47) in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in New York.
items.imageAlt: Ciryl Gane weighing in at the UFC Freedom 250 ceremonial weigh-in, Washington, June 2026

items.title: Australia and the Philippines sign a new defence agreement in Manila
items.summary: Australia and the Philippines signed a new agreement in Manila on Sunday, 15 November, to strengthen military cooperation, as the Philippines is locked in a serious dispute with China in the South China Sea.
items.imageAlt: Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro at the Western Command headquarters in Palawan, November 2024

items.title: Iran: three oil tankers hit mines in Hormuz as Bahrain sounds warning sirens
items.summary: The IRGC Navy said two oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, while warning sirens sounded in Bahrain on Sunday, 15 November.
items.imageAlt: IRGC Navy commandos and missile boats near the Strait of Hormuz during a 2015 exercise

items.title: UFC 334: Kayla Harrison chokes out Amanda Nunes in the fourth round to retain her title
items.summary: Kayla Harrison defended her UFC bantamweight championship by submitting Amanda Nunes with a choke in the fourth round on Saturday night at Madison Square Garden in New York.
items.imageAlt: Kayla Harrison celebrating after winning the judo gold medal at the Rio 2016 Olympics

items.title: Saudi Arabia says it shot down two missiles fired at Riyadh by the Houthis
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences on Sunday, 15 November, shot down two ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis at the capital Riyadh.
items.imageAlt: The skyline of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

items.title: Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G 3-1 to win the League of Legends World Championship
items.summary: Chinese team Bilibili Gaming (BLG) beat South Korea's Gen.G 3-1 in the final of the League of Legends esports World Championship at the Barclays Center in New York, ending South Korea's run of 4 straight titles.
items.imageAlt: Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, where the final was played

items.title: SpaceX catches a Starship returning from space with launch tower arms for the first time
items.summary: SpaceX on Saturday, 14 November, for the first time in history caught its Starship spacecraft with the giant arms of the launch tower at Starbase, Texas, after it returned from a journey around the Earth.
items.imageAlt: SpaceX's Starship standing on the launch mount at Starbase, Texas, April 2023

items.title: Netanyahu calls for a unity government, Eisenkot dismisses it as a trick
items.summary: Israel's caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday, 14 November, again called for him and Gadi Eisenkot to form a national unity government, while Eisenkot described the appeal as a trick.
items.imageAlt: Benjamin Netanyahu, official photo taken in February 2023

items.title: Mirra Andreeva beats Pegula to reach the WTA Finals final
items.summary: Russian player Mirra Andreeva beat Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 in the WTA Finals semi-final in Indian Wells and became the youngest player to reach the final of the event in 22 years.
items.imageAlt: File photo: Mirra Andreeva playing at the 2023 US Open

items.title: Iraqi prime minister dismisses nine officials suspected of oil smuggling
items.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on Saturday, 14 November, dismissed nine officials and ordered that everyone accused of oil smuggling in Jurf al-Sakher be referred to the judiciary.
items.imageAlt: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi at the Pentagon, Washington, 14 July 2026

items.title: France: 106,000 join cost-of-living protests on the fifth Saturday in a row
items.summary: About 106,000 people held protests against the cost of living in French cities on Saturday, 14 November, including 24,000 in Paris, the interior minister said, while student unions put the figure at 200,000.
items.imageAlt: Archive photo: a Yellow Vest protest in Paris, 9 February 2019

items.title: Kalonzo Musyoka says he will back the Kenyan opposition's joint candidate in the 2027 election
items.summary: Wiper party leader Kalonzo Musyoka said on Saturday he is ready to give up his presidential ambitions to support a single candidate fielded by the opposition in Kenya's 2027 general election.
items.imageAlt: Kalonzo Musyoka, leader of Kenya's Wiper party (file photo)

items.title: Rugby: Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 for first win since 1953
items.summary: Wales's rugby team beat New Zealand 35-28 in Cardiff on Saturday in the Nations Championship, their first victory over the All Blacks in 73 years.
items.imageAlt: The Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales

items.title: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros for accessing users' photos without consent
items.summary: Italy's data protection authority on Saturday fined Meta, the owner of Facebook, 805 million euros, accusing it of accessing users' photos and videos through the Facebook Android app without their specific consent.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the Facebook (Meta) campus in Menlo Park, California

items.title: Somalia and Türkiye sign agreement in Antalya to strengthen family protection and social services
items.summary: Somalia's Minister of Family and Human Rights Development, Khadija Mohamed Al-Makhzoumi, and her Turkish counterpart, Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş, signed a memorandum of understanding in Antalya on social services and the protection of families.
items.imageAlt: Türkiye's Minister of Family and Social Services, Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş, at a conference in Budapest in 2023

items.title: Mohamed Salah becomes Egypt's all-time top scorer
items.summary: Former Liverpool star Mohamed Salah has become the highest scorer in the history of Egypt's national team after scoring twice in a 5-0 win over Malawi in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.
items.imageAlt: Mohamed Salah playing for Egypt in the Argentina v Egypt match at the 2026 World Cup

items.title: Bulgaria stops supplying Ukraine with weapons from its army stocks
items.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said his country will no longer give Ukraine weapons and ammunition taken from army stocks and will not contribute to new European Union financing.
items.imageAlt: Rumen Radev speaking at a conference in Budapest in 2023

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh alone in the National Dialogue Forum hall, with the seats prepared for participants empty
items.summary: A photo taken at the venue prepared for the National Dialogue Forum shows President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud sitting alone at the conference's central table, while the other seats in the hall are empty.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud sitting alone at the central table in the National Dialogue Forum hall, with the other seats empty

items.title: Kenya: fuel prices unchanged for the coming month, EPRA says
items.summary: Kenya's Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) announced that prices of petrol, diesel and kerosene will remain unchanged from 14 November to 15 December, with the government paying a subsidy.
items.imageAlt: A fuel station on the A104 road in Nairobi, Kenya

items.title: Medical oxygen plant opened at Baraawe General Hospital
items.summary: The leader of South West State, Sheikh Adan Mohamed Nur (Madobe), on Saturday, 14 November, cut the ribbon on a new plant producing medical oxygen built at the General Hospital of Baraawe district.
items.imageAlt: Fishermen off the coast of Baraawe in the Lower Shabelle region, 2022

items.title: Somalia and India open their first foreign ministry consultations in Mogadishu
items.summary: The Federal Government of Somalia and the Government of India on Saturday, 14 November, began in Mogadishu the first formal consultations between the two countries' foreign ministries.
items.imageAlt: Sripriya Ranganathan of India's Ministry of External Affairs climbing aboard the vessel Dali in Baltimore in 2024, when she was a diplomat at India's embassy in the United States

items.title: South Sudan and Sudan sign deal in Khartoum on crude oil volumes
items.summary: South Sudan and Sudan have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in Khartoum to reconcile the two countries' crude oil volumes and strengthen cooperation in the petroleum sector, Eye Radio reported on Saturday 14 November.
items.imageAlt: The oil export terminal at Port Sudan seen from a ship, 2019 (archive photo)

items.title: Zelensky: US floated Ukraine leaving Donbas in exchange for NATO membership
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said US negotiators floated the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its forces from the part of Donbas it still holds in exchange for joining NATO, the BBC and other media reported on Saturday 14 November.
items.imageAlt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky during a visit to the Council of Europe in Strasbourg, June 2025 (archive photo)

items.title: Erdoğan urges Hassan Sheikh to pursue political dialogue and national unity
items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan spoke to President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud about the importance of national unity and of political dialogue to resolve Somalia's dispute, according to a statement from the Turkish Presidency cited by Hiiraan Online on Saturday 14 November.
items.imageAlt: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud listen to the national anthems at Aden Adde airport in Mogadishu, 2015 (archive photo)

items.title: Ahmed Madobe appoints Mukhtar Sheikh Ahmed Abdulle as Jubaland's Second Vice President
items.summary: Jubaland President Ahmed Mohamed Islam (Ahmed Madobe) issued a decree in Kismayo on Saturday 14 November appointing Mukhtar Sheikh Ahmed Abdulle as Second Vice President of Jubaland.
items.imageAlt: Jubaland President Ahmed Mohamed Islam (Ahmed Madobe) speaking at a meeting in Mogadishu, 2021 (archive photo)

items.title: UN Security Council extends Abyei peacekeeping mission until November 2027
items.summary: The UN Security Council on Friday, 13 November, extended the mandate of the UN Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) by another year, until 15 November 2027, with China and Russia abstaining.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the Abyei area, 2009 (archive photo)

items.title: South Sudan: Elections commission postpones general elections to 11 February 2027
items.summary: South Sudan's National Elections Commission (NEC) has postponed the country's general elections to 11 February 2027, instead of 22 December 2026, according to a revised calendar obtained by Radio Tamazuj, which was also reported by Eye Radio.
items.imageAlt: People voting in Lainya, South Sudan, 2011 (archive photo)

items.title: Somali presidency: National Consultative Forum to open soon
items.summary: The Presidency of the Federal Republic of Somalia said on Saturday, 14 November, that contacts are under way with the parties invited to the National Consultative Forum, which it said will open soon, state broadcaster Radio Muqdisho reported.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud at Villa Somalia in Mogadishu, 2014 (archive photo)

items.title: Somali government responds to UN experts' condemnation of the Chief Justice's removal
items.summary: Somalia's Federal Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs on Saturday, 14 November, formally responded to a statement in which UN experts on 12 November condemned the removal of the former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, saying it is committed to protecting the independence of the judiciary.
items.imageAlt: Judicial officials and diplomats at the opening of the Banadir Regional Court in Mogadishu, 2015 (archive photo)

items.title: Rugby: France beat South Africa 21-19 at the Stade de France
items.summary: France's rugby team beat South Africa, winners of the last two World Cups, 21-19 at the Stade de France in Paris on Friday, 13 November, in a 5th-round match of the Nations Championship.
items.imageAlt: Fans at the Stade de France in Paris during a rugby match (archive photo)

items.title: Kenya: six coastal counties urged to strengthen tsunami preparedness
items.summary: Kenya's National Disaster Operations Centre (NDOC) has urged the country's six coastal counties to hold regular tsunami drills in schools, tourism establishments and fishing communities.
items.imageAlt: Diani beach on Kenya's coast (file photo)

items.title: French-speaking nations' summit opens in Cambodia overshadowed by Rwanda-Congo dispute
items.summary: The biennial summit of the International Organisation of La Francophonie began on Saturday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with the election of the organisation's secretary-general dividing Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, the AP news agency reported.
items.imageAlt: Louise Mushikiwabo, the current Francophonie secretary-general, when she was Rwanda's foreign minister (file photo)

items.title: Svitolina fights back to beat Muchova and keep WTA Finals hopes alive
items.summary: Ukraine's Elina Svitolina beat Karolina Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 at the WTA Finals, keeping alive her chance of reaching the semi-finals.
items.imageAlt: Elina Svitolina during a tennis match

items.title: US judge allows Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the BBC to proceed
items.summary: A federal judge in Florida has ruled that President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the BBC, in which he seeks $10 billion, can proceed.
items.imageAlt: The BBC's Broadcasting House headquarters in London

items.title: Somali government: ready for technical compromise, but no retreat on one-person-one-vote elections
items.summary: Somalia's Information Minister, Abdifatah Qasim Mohamud, said the federal government is ready to compromise on technical aspects of the elections but will not back down on holding one-person-one-vote elections.
items.imageAlt: Somalia's presidential palace, Villa Somalia, in Mogadishu

items.title: South Sudan declares Friday a public holiday for General Joseph Lagu's state funeral
items.summary: South Sudan has declared Friday, 13 November 2026, a public holiday so that citizens can attend the state funeral of General Joseph Lagu Yanga, leader of the Anyanya movement, the high-level state funeral committee said.
items.imageAlt: The Dr John Garang Mausoleum square in Juba, South Sudan

items.title: United States pulls its team out of the U-17 World Cup in Qatar over security concerns
items.summary: U.S. Soccer has decided not to send its under-17 national team to the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar, citing security concerns linked to the conflict in the Middle East.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the Aspire Zone sports complex in Doha, Qatar

items.title: Press release: Nabad iyo Nolol party says it did not take part in a joint opposition meeting
items.summary: In a press release, the Nabad iyo Nolol party says reports that it took part in a joint meeting with other opposition groups are false, and describes a visit by the commanders of the armed forces to the home of the 9th President, Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo.
items.imageAlt: The Nabad iyo Nolol party's press release of 11 November 2026, signed by party spokesperson Cabdirashiid Maxamed Xaashi

items.title: Iran designates Argentina's navy and air force as terrorist organisations
items.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry announced on Wednesday that it has designated Argentina's navy and air force as terrorist organisations, in response to an earlier decision by Buenos Aires against Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
items.imageAlt: Argentine Navy corvettes ARA Robinson and ARA Rosales

items.title: Hassan Sheikh urges polluting nations at COP31 to lead the response to climate change
items.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on Wednesday addressed the 31st UN climate change conference (COP31), which opened in Antalya, Türkiye, and called on the international community to honour its climate commitments.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud speaking at the Global Food Security Summit in London, November 2023

items.title: The Hassan Sheikh–Abiy meeting: sea access and Somalia's sovereignty
items.summary: Today's meeting in Türkiye between President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed came at a time when the two countries still face diplomatic challenges arising from the dispute over sea access. Somalia's principle is that its sovereignty and territorial unity must be fully respected.
items.imageAlt: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan speaking at an AK Parti event (file photo, not from today's meeting)

items.title: Somalia and Germany: 66 years of diplomatic relations, cooperation and friendship
items.summary: Somalia and Germany have had diplomatic relations since Somalia gained independence on 1 July 1960, built on friendship, mutual respect, cooperation and the interests of both peoples. By Eng Mahad AA.
items.imageAlt: The flag of Germany (left) and the flag of Somalia (right), with the Wartabiye TV logo

items.title: Former NFL coach Rex Ryan charged after pedestrian incident in Nashville
items.summary: Rex Ryan, the ESPN analyst and former head coach of the New York Jets and Buffalo Bills, turned himself in to Nashville police on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, after being accused of hitting two pedestrians with his car and leaving the scene.
items.imageAlt: Broadway in downtown Nashville, Tennessee

items.title: Turkish Ambassador Ferhat Alkan meets former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire
items.summary: Türkiye's Ambassador to Somalia, Ferhat Alkan, held a courtesy meeting with Hassan Ali Khaire, Somalia's 19th Prime Minister. They discussed the country's political process, the efforts of the Quartet of Türkiye, the United States, the United Kingdom and the European Union, and relations between Türkiye and Somalia.
items.imageAlt: Turkish Ambassador Ferhat Alkan (left) and former Somali Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire (right) standing side by side, with Somali flags behind them

items.title: Russia's ambassador to the US, Alexander Darchiev, dies at 66
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry announced on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, that the country's ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, had died suddenly at the age of 66.
items.imageAlt: The Russian embassy building in Washington, D.C.

items.title: Iran threatens to strike US bases in Europe if they are used to attack it
items.summary: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, that Tehran would strike US bases in Europe and on distant islands if they were used to launch an attack on Iran.
items.imageAlt: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council (2013 photo)

items.title: Kenya's parliament passes law barring hospitals from detaining patients and bodies
items.summary: Kenya's National Assembly on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, passed a law that prohibits hospitals from demanding upfront payment from patients in emergencies, or from holding patients and bodies over unpaid bills.
items.imageAlt: The chamber of Kenya's National Assembly in Nairobi

items.title: IGAD's Somalia representative receives Sweden's ambassador in Mogadishu
items.summary: IGAD's Representative to Somalia, Mohamud Karshe, received Sweden's Ambassador to Somalia, H.E. Amb. Hans Henric Lundquist, at the IGAD office in Mogadishu, where they discussed strengthening cooperation on peace, security and stability.
items.imageAlt: IGAD Representative to Somalia Mohamud Karshe and Swedish Ambassador Hans Henric Lundquist at the IGAD office in Mogadishu

items.title: England women cancel West Indies Test to prepare for the Ashes
items.summary: England's women's cricket team have cancelled a Test that was due to be played in the West Indies in April and will instead play red-ball matches in England to prepare for the Ashes.
items.imageAlt: A building at Headingley cricket ground in Leeds, England

items.title: Somalia's justice minister warns of threat to statehood, calls for review of federal system
items.summary: Somalia's Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Hassan Macallin Mohamud, warned on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, of the political and security dangers facing the country and called for the federal system to be reviewed.
items.imageAlt: Politicians and Somali elders at Villa Somalia during the signing of the Baidoa federal state agreement (2014 photo)

items.title: Trump's envoys head to Moscow to see Putin after Abu Dhabi talks end without clear progress
items.summary: Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, said on Wednesday that he and Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow tomorrow to meet President Vladimir Putin, after trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a clear breakthrough.
items.imageAlt: Russian President Vladimir Putin shaking hands with US envoy Steve Witkoff, 5 September 2026

items.title: Spain holds its first general strike in 14 years over the housing crisis
items.summary: Millions of workers in Spain began a 24-hour general strike on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, demanding that the government tackle the housing crisis, less than three weeks before the 29 November national election.
items.imageAlt: Posters calling for the general strike of 14 November 2012 on a street in Barcelona (archive photo)

items.title: Kenya discharges its last Ebola patient, starting a 42-day countdown to being declared free of the disease
items.summary: Kenya on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, discharged its last Ebola patient from hospital, beginning a 42-day monitoring period; if no new cases are found, the country will be declared Ebola-free on 23 December, Health Minister Aden Duale said.
items.imageAlt: Aden Duale, then Kenya's Defence Cabinet Secretary, speaking at Manda Bay, September 2023

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh and Prime Minister Abiy discuss the security of Somalia and the region in Türkiye
items.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed met in Türkiye ahead of the COP31 leaders' summit in the city of Antalya and discussed the security situation in Somalia and developments in the Horn of Africa, Ethiopian state media outlet Fana reported.
items.imageAlt: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed at the inauguration ceremony of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in Mogadishu, June 2022

items.title: Somaliland executes nine prisoners sentenced to death by its courts for murder
items.summary: The Somaliland administration on Wednesday morning, 11 November 2026, carried out death sentences in the Mandheera area on nine people whom Somaliland's courts had earlier sentenced to death after convicting them of murder.
items.imageAlt: The war memorial in central Hargeisa, the capital of Somaliland (photo 2007)

items.title: Somalia and Saudi Arabia sign 2027 Hajj agreement: Somalia allocated 11,500 pilgrims
items.summary: The Federal Government of Somalia and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia signed the Hajj quota agreement for the year 1448 AH (2027) in Jeddah, allocating Somalia 11,500 pilgrims.
items.imageAlt: Somalia's Minister of Endowments and Religious Affairs, Sheikh Mukhtar Robow Ali, attending a conference in Mogadishu, January 2023

items.title: Lithuania closes Vilnius and Kaunas airports and NATO scrambles jets after drones from Belarus
items.summary: NATO fighter jets were scrambled twice overnight after suspected drones believed to have come from Belarus triggered air alerts across large parts of Lithuania, and the Vilnius and Kaunas airports were temporarily closed, Türkiye Today reported, citing Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT.
items.imageAlt: The main entrance of Vilnius International Airport, Lithuania

items.summary: US Africa Command (AFRICOM) has for the first time formally confirmed that US troops have left the Baledogle military base in the Lower Shabelle region after its runway deteriorated.

items.title: Heads of security agencies meet opposition leaders in Mogadishu
items.summary: The commanders of Somalia's security and military agencies have met opposition leaders in Mogadishu in talks focused on the country's security situation and political tension.
items.imageAlt: Former prime minister Mohamed Hussein Roble speaking at a conference in Mogadishu, December 2020

items.title: Senator Ted Cruz ties support for new US ambassador to Somalia to the Somaliland question
items.summary: US Senator Ted Cruz has said his support for confirming Devin Kennington, whom President Donald Trump nominated as US ambassador to Somalia, depends on how the administration acts on the president's position on Somaliland.
items.imageAlt: Senator Ted Cruz, official US Senate portrait (2019)

items.title: Uganda and East African lawyers' bodies urge Hassan Sheikh to respect Supreme Court
items.summary: The Uganda Law Society and the East Africa Law Society (EALS) called on President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in statements issued on 10 November 2026 to respect the rulings of Somalia's Supreme Court.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud giving a speech in Mogadishu (2012 photo)

items.summary: Pirate attacks off Somalia's coast have been increasing again since April 2026, according to a report published on 10 November by Africa Defense Forum, raising concern over the safety of merchant ships in the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.

items.title: Kenya: Senate committee concerned over Kasarani stadium's readiness for AFCON 2027
items.summary: The Kenyan Senate's Committee on Labour and Social Welfare has raised concerns over the readiness of the Moi International Sports Centre, Kasarani, which is due to host matches at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).

items.title: Ebola: cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo pass 11,000, with 5,387 deaths

items.imageAlt: Congolese Red Cross volunteers in Bunia, Ituri province, during the Ebola outbreak, August 2026

items.title: Russia says it downed 146 drones over the Leningrad region

items.imageAlt: The office of the KINEF oil refining company in the town of Kirishi, Leningrad region

items.title: El Salvador says it destroyed the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo gang in Haiti

items.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah back in court today, facing possible prison

items.title: Russia expels a Moldovan diplomat in response to a move by Chisinau

items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on Tuesday received six leaders and officials in Antalya, where the COP31 climate conference is under way, and witnessed the signing of an electricity memorandum of understanding between Türkiye and Saudi Arabia.

items.title: US House begins a vote deciding the fate of the resolution to impeach Hegseth
items.summary: The US House of Representatives on Tuesday began a procedural vote to decide whether the resolution to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is sent back to committee or moves to a final vote.

items.summary: Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton, a 7-time world champion, on Tuesday visited the Egyptian city of El Arish and the Rafah crossing, where he met aid workers preparing assistance for the Gaza Strip.

items.summary: A new indictment issued by US federal prosecutors accuses Mohammad Dawood Al-Saadi, who holds Iranian and Iraqi citizenship, of directing from a New York jail a failed plot to attack the RAF Fairford air base in Britain.

items.summary: Iran says it has not suspended its obligations under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), but broad international inspections of its sites remain far off.

items.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty has said that Egyptian soldiers have been in Saudi Arabia for many months to protect key sites after attacks on the kingdom, noting that the forces will not cross into Yemen.

items.summary: The Speaker of Uganda's Parliament, Jacob Oboth, has directed the science and technology committee to investigate within two weeks the government's 723.4 billion shilling investment in the company Dei BioPharma.

items.summary: Türkiye's Ambassador to Somalia, Ferhat Alkan, held a courtesy meeting with Somalia's 9th President, Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed Farmaajo. The two discussed the situation in Somalia, Türkiye–Somalia relations and regional and global affairs, according to a statement from the Turkish Embassy.
items.imageAlt: Turkish Ambassador Ferhat Alkan (left) and former Somali President Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo (right) standing side by side, with the Somali flag behind them

items.title: FIFPro: 5 Spanish players in the women's world best team of 2026
items.summary: The professional footballers' union FIFPro has announced the women's FIFPro World 11 of 2026, voted by 6511 professional players from 64 countries; it includes Irene Paredes, Mapi León, Aitana Bonmatí, Alexia Putellas and Claudia Pina.
items.imageAlt: Footballer Aitana Bonmatí on the pitch

items.title: France: Lecornu brings forward 1.6% minimum wage increase
items.summary: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a 1.6% minimum wage increase planned for January will be brought forward to December, after talks with trade unions and business leaders, as the country faces protests over the cost of living; unions said the increase falls short of their demands.
items.imageAlt: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu

items.title: NFL: Jacksonville Jaguars acquire Jessie Bates III from Atlanta Falcons
items.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have reached a deal with the Atlanta Falcons, ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, to acquire All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III, with the Falcons receiving a round 2 pick in 2027 and a round 5 pick in 2028.
items.imageAlt: NFL player Jessie Bates III

items.title: Kenya: Victor Wanyama to captain Harambee Stars legends against Arsenal
items.summary: Former Harambee Stars captain Victor Wanyama will lead Kenya's legends against Arsenal's legends in the Legends Cup at Nyayo Stadium on Friday, alongside MacDonald Mariga and Dennis Oliech.
items.imageAlt: Kenyan footballer Victor Wanyama

items.title: Kremlin rejects European participation in Abu Dhabi talks
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday that this week's peace meeting in Abu Dhabi, attended by Ukrainian and US representatives, will not include European Union officials, noting that the United States and Ukraine have their own channels for communicating with the Europeans.
items.imageAlt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov

items.title: South Sudan: Yei police arrest man suspected of killing secondary school student
items.summary: Police in Yei River County have arrested a man suspected of killing Henry Dengero, a Senior 2 student at Yei Day Secondary School, who was reportedly shot by robbers who then took his motorcycle on Friday night, county police inspector Yoasa Lujang Kamba said.
items.imageAlt: A road in the central business area of Yei, South Sudan

items.title: Uganda: Minister Justine Lumumba calls for technology to reach rural areas
items.summary: Uganda's Minister of ICT and National Guidance, Justine Lumumba, visited the Buhadyo Smart Village project in Butaleja district on Saturday and urged rural communities to adopt technology widely to narrow the digital divide.
items.imageAlt: Minister Justine Kasule Lumumba

items.title: Kenya: Ronald Karauri joins UDA to challenge Sakaja for Nairobi governor
items.summary: Kasarani MP Ronald Karauri has officially joined the ruling UDA party to run for governor of Nairobi county in the 2027 election. The move comes days after Governor Johnson Sakaja left UDA for the ODM party.
items.imageAlt: Ronald Karauri

items.title: Trump says dislike of Israel was among reasons Republicans were defeated
items.summary: President Donald Trump said in an interview with CBS's "60 Minutes" that the Iran war, rising fuel prices and a dislike of Israel were among the reasons Republicans lost the midterm elections.
items.imageAlt: President Donald Trump during a 60 Minutes interview (2025)

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh attends COP31 climate summit in Antalya
items.summary: Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud is attending the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), which opened on Monday in the Turkish city of Antalya.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud speaking at a meeting in London, May 2013

items.title: Alisson says he wants to stay at Liverpool
items.summary: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson, whose contract expires at the end of this season, said his wish is to stay at Anfield, after Sunday's 3-1 win at Crystal Palace.
items.imageAlt: Goalkeeper Alisson playing for Brazil in a 2018 friendly

items.title: Uganda: Central Bank holds its policy rate at 12%
items.summary: The Bank of Uganda has held its Central Bank Rate (CBR) at 12%, warning that energy prices, a weaker shilling and bad weather could push inflation higher, Governor Michael Atingi-Ego said. The bank also widened the CBR band to 3 percentage points.
items.imageAlt: The headquarters of the Bank of Uganda in Kampala

items.title: Kenya: Ruto mocks opposition leaders claiming millions of votes
items.summary: President William Ruto has questioned claims by Rigathi Gachagua, Kalonzo Musyoka and Fred Matiang'i that they command millions of votes, after a meeting they held in Nairobi this week about the 2027 election. Ruto made the remarks during a tour of the Gusii region.
items.imageAlt: President William Ruto addressing the public in Meru County

items.title: Greece: At least 21 migrants die trying to reach Crete
items.summary: Greece's coastguard said at least 21 people died trying to reach the island of Crete, while more than 100 people were rescued in several operations off the south of the island.
items.imageAlt: Hellenic Coast Guard office at the port of Heraklion, Crete

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh opens new Hirshabelle buildings in Jowhar
items.summary: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on Monday opened the new headquarters of the Hirshabelle House of Representatives and the state's Ministry of Security in Jowhar.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the town of Jowhar and the surrounding farmland

items.title: Hassan Ali Khaire accuses two officers of killings and land grabbing in Raadeerka, Deyniile
items.summary: Former Somali Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire used his Facebook page to condemn what he called a massacre, land grabbing and forced displacement in the Raadeerka neighbourhood of Deyniile district, blaming two officers he named. Neither the officers nor the government has yet responded to the accusations.
items.imageAlt: A composite image circulated on social media showing two police officers said to be the officers named by Hassan Ali Khaire

items.title: Cricket: England open door for Brydon Carse return and drop Shoaib Bashir
items.summary: England named Brydon Carse in the Lions squad, opening the way for his return to Tests on the South Africa tour, while in the 15-man squad for the 3-Test series starting in Johannesburg on 17 December Liam Patterson-White replaced Shoaib Bashir.
items.imageAlt: England cricketer Brydon Carse

items.title: Kenya: Murkomen urges Sifuna to back Ruto, promises him leadership in 2032
items.summary: Kenya's Interior Minister Kipchumba Murkomen has urged Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna to drop his presidential ambitions for the 2027 election and back President William Ruto, saying the Luhya community could in that way take the country's leadership in 2032.
items.imageAlt: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, 2024

items.title: Pierre Kalulu to miss France's Nations League matches through injury
items.summary: Tests carried out after Juventus' match against Fiorentina showed that defender Pierre Kalulu has a muscle injury in his left leg, so he will not take part in France's matches against Italy and Turkey.
items.imageAlt: Defender Pierre Kalulu, 2022

items.title: South Sudan: Gen. Joseph Lagu to be buried at Dr John Garang's mausoleum in Juba
items.summary: The organising committee for the state funeral of General Joseph Lagu Yanga, leader of the Anyanya One movement, told Eye Radio that he will be buried inside the Dr John Garang mausoleum in the city of Juba, after President Salva Kiir decided that he should be given a state funeral.
items.imageAlt: General Joseph Lagu arriving at the Dr John Garang mausoleum in Juba, 9 July 2011

items.title: Judo legend Teddy Riner to run for French president in 2027
items.summary: Teddy Riner, who has won 5 Olympic gold medals, announced on Monday that he will run in France's 2027 presidential election.
items.imageAlt: Teddy Riner, the French judo legend

items.title: Trump: "We won in Iran", as US forces strike Qeshm Island
items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that the United States has "won" the Iran war and that renewed fighting is unlikely if Tehran reaches a deal, as US forces struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
items.imageAlt: President Donald Trump in the Oval Office

items.title: Uganda: CAA senior engineer and 10 others brought to court after vandalism at Entebbe airport
items.summary: 11 officials of the Uganda Civil Aviation Authority, including senior engineer Herbert Ngobi, were brought before the Entebbe High Court on Monday, charged with negligence of duty linked to the vandalism of airport equipment worth Shs3.7 billion.
items.imageAlt: Entebbe International Airport, Uganda

items.title: Golf: 19-year-old Blades Brown becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years
items.summary: American golfer Blades Brown, 19, won the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico, beating Ben James on the second play-off hole to become the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years.
items.imageAlt: American golfer Blades Brown

items.title: Iran: IAEA inspectors recently visited the Bushehr nuclear plant
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) recently visited the Bushehr nuclear power plant, calling it evidence that cooperation with the agency continues.
items.imageAlt: The Bushehr nuclear power plant, Iran

items.title: Guterres: The world has entered an 'age of climate extremes'
items.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Monday urged leaders gathered at COP31 in Antalya to speed up emissions cuts and the transition away from fossil fuels, saying the world has entered 'a new age of climate extremes'.
items.imageAlt: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres

items.title: Tanzania and the WTTC discuss attracting tourism investment in London
items.summary: Tanzania's Minister of Natural Resources and Tourism, Dr Ashatu Kijaji, met the chairman of the World Travel and Tourism Council (WTTC), Manfredi Lefebvre, in London, and they discussed tourism investment and increasing international visitors.
items.imageAlt: Manfredi Lefebvre, chairman of the WTTC (photo 2015)

items.title: IGAD and Germany hold their annual cooperation dialogue in Djibouti
items.summary: IGAD and the German government held their annual cooperation dialogue on Monday at IGAD headquarters in Djibouti and reaffirmed their commitment to peace, resilience and regional integration in the Horn of Africa, according to a statement from IGAD. The IGAD delegation was led by Executive Secretary Dr Workneh…
items.imageAlt: IGAD Executive Secretary Workneh Gebeyehu (2018 photo)

items.title: Ethiopia opens its own pavilion at the COP31 summit in Antalya as it prepares to host COP32
items.summary: Ethiopia's Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos and Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa opened Ethiopia's pavilion at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, as the country prepares to host COP32 in 2027, state-affiliated Fana reported.
items.imageAlt: Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos

items.title: Speaker Wetang'ula steps up Ruto's re-election campaign in western Kenya
items.summary: Kenya's National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula has urged people in western Kenya to back President William Ruto, who is seeking a second term in the 2027 general election, saying the alliance will strengthen the region's influence in government.
items.imageAlt: Kenya's National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula

items.title: Nairobi steps up water rationing after levels at Ndakaini Dam fall
items.summary: The Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company said water rationing has been stepped up because output at the Ngethu and Kigoro plants has fallen by 35% after water levels at Ndakaini Dam dropped; parts of Kiambu, Kajiado and Machakos will be affected.
items.imageAlt: Ndakaini Dam near Thika, Kenya

items.title: Museveni urges Uganda's universities to prioritise skills training
items.summary: President Yoweri Museveni has urged Uganda's universities to focus on hands-on skills training so that students can create jobs, saying unemployment is a major challenge; the speech was read at Bugema University by Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni

items.title: Bank of Tanzania: guarantees of 1.6 trillion opened 2.1 trillion shillings in loans to businesses
items.summary: The Bank of Tanzania (BoT) said it has issued loan guarantees totalling 1.6 trillion shillings, which made it easier for businesses to obtain loans totalling 2.1 trillion shillings across various sectors of the economy, the state-owned Daily News reported.
items.imageAlt: The Bank of Tanzania headquarters in Dar es Salaam

items.title: USA and Pacific Islands to host 2030 Rugby League World Cup
items.summary: International Rugby League (IRL) has decided the 2030 World Cup will be held in the USA and the Pacific Islands, with the 5 host cities yet to be announced.
items.imageAlt: The Rugby League World Cup trophy on display

items.title: Netherlands: Vitesse v De Graafschap called off after fans block their team's bus
items.summary: A Dutch second-tier match between Vitesse Arnhem and De Graafschap was called off after De Graafschap supporters stopped their own team's bus from leaving for the game.
items.imageAlt: The GelreDome stadium in Arnhem, Netherlands

items.title: Kenyan police seize 454 kg of methamphetamine
items.summary: Kenyan police say they seized 454 kg of methamphetamine worth an estimated $27 million on the country's coast and arrested 3 suspects.
items.imageAlt: A sample of crystal methamphetamine (illustrative photo)

items.title: Trump says he will meet Putin and Xi in China
items.summary: President Donald Trump said he expects to meet Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November, saying they would discuss nuclear disarmament and ending the Iran war.
items.imageAlt: Xi Jinping during the welcome ceremony for Donald Trump in China, May 2026

items.title: Huckabee: US aid to Israel will not be cut off abruptly
items.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee said Washington's $4 billion in aid would not be cut off suddenly, since ending it requires approval from Congress, Türkiye Today reported, citing i24NEWS.
items.imageAlt: Mike Huckabee speaking in Des Moines, Iowa

items.title: Law Society of Kenya demands accountability as lawyer Abshir remains missing
items.summary: The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) has called on the security agencies to disclose the whereabouts of lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi and announced new protests on Tuesday, the day the High Court in Milimani is due to rule on the habeas corpus case.
items.imageAlt: A Kenyan judiciary building in Nairobi

items.title: Tanzania: STAMICO opens a clean fuel plant in Dodoma costing 3.7 billion shillings
items.summary: The State Mining Corporation of Tanzania (STAMICO) has opened the Rafiki Briquettes plant in the city of Dodoma, which cost 3.7 billion shillings, to reduce reliance on firewood and charcoal.
items.imageAlt: The centre of the city of Dodoma, Tanzania

items.title: Krakow: Suspected gunman who killed 6 people dies in hospital
items.summary: Polish police said the 24-year-old man suspected of killing at least 6 people in a shooting in central Krakow on Saturday died in hospital early on Monday.
items.imageAlt: The Town Hall Tower and Cloth Hall on Krakow's Main Market Square

items.title: TikTok removes more than 750,000 videos in Kenya
items.summary: TikTok said it removed 750,185 videos in Kenya that violated its community guidelines between April and June 2026.
items.imageAlt: The TikTok app on a mobile phone

items.title: Vodacom Tanzania profit rises 183 percent
items.summary: Vodacom Tanzania said its net profit reached 117.8 billion shillings in the six months to September 2026, while service revenue rose 20.8 percent to 1.067 trillion shillings.
items.imageAlt: An M-Pesa agent in Tanzania

items.title: Asian stock markets rebound after tech sell-off
items.summary: Asian stock markets rose on Monday after last week's fall linked to the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections, with Tokyo's Nikkei 225 up 3.45%.
items.imageAlt: The Tokyo Stock Exchange building in Japan

items.title: Rubio: War on Iran is unpopular but was necessary to stop the nuclear threat
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that President Trump launched the war on Iran to protect the world from Tehran's nuclear ambitions, adding that talks are not close to a breakthrough.
items.imageAlt: Marco Rubio speaking at an event

items.title: Somalia, Egypt and Djibouti say Red Sea security belongs to the coastal states
items.summary: The foreign ministers of Somalia, Egypt and Djibouti pledged on Monday in Tripoli, Libya, that securing the Red Sea is the responsibility of the states on its coasts.
items.imageAlt: Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, February 2025

items.title: Mexico arrests man suspected of being a senior leader of the Jalisco drug cartel
items.summary: Mexico's Navy said Rafael Alvarez, known as "R2", who is suspected of heading a cell of the CJNG cartel, was arrested on Sunday in the city of Zapopan using intelligence provided by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).
items.imageAlt: Omar García Harfuch, Mexico's security minister

items.title: New Delhi engulfed by toxic smog after Diwali celebrations
items.summary: A cloud of smoke and pollution covered India's capital on Monday morning after people set off firecrackers on Sunday to celebrate Diwali, with the air quality index (AQI) exceeding 350 in many parts of the city.
items.imageAlt: Smog covering the sky over Delhi

items.title: Drone attack hits industrial area in Russia's Kirishi
items.summary: Leningrad Region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Telegram that drones attacked an industrial area in the city of Kirishi, about 150 km from St. Petersburg, overnight, and that 113 drones were shot down, the TT news agency reported via Sweden Herald.
items.imageAlt: The KINEF company office in Kirishi, Russia

items.title: Moldova launches new power line to Romania to reduce reliance on Russia
items.summary: Moldova on Sunday officially launched a new power line linking the country to Romania and the European electricity grid, Al Jazeera reported, with the aim of reducing its reliance on Russian energy.
items.imageAlt: Moldovan President Maia Sandu

items.title: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris; Europe to press the US on Ukraine and Iran
items.summary: G7 foreign ministers begin 2 days of talks in Paris on Monday, and France 24 reported that European countries will press the United States to seek a fair settlement for Ukraine and to refrain from new strikes on Iran.
items.imageAlt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio

items.title: Trump says offering Dana White the press secretary job was a joke
items.summary: President Donald Trump told The New York Times that his offer of the White House press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White was not serious, saying "I was just kidding", Sweden Herald reported, citing the TT news agency.
items.imageAlt: Dana White, head of the UFC

items.title: Biden: Cancer will limit the conversations I can have about my book
items.summary: Former US President Joe Biden said on social media on Sunday that his cancer will prevent him from doing as many conversations promoting his memoir as he had hoped.
items.imageAlt: Portrait of Joe Biden, former President of the United States

items.title: Hakeem Jeffries backs impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
items.summary: US House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said he fully supports a resolution seeking to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, whom he accused of engineering the war in Iran.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic leader in the US House of Representatives

items.title: Merz to name Ilse Aigner as presidential candidate, Germany's first woman head of state if elected
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Sunday he will nominate Ilse Aigner, speaker of the Bavarian state parliament, as the CDU and CSU candidate for German president, Al Jazeera reported; if elected, she would be the country's first female head of state.
items.imageAlt: Ilse Aigner, speaker of the Bavarian state parliament

items.title: COP31 climate summit opens today in Antalya; Aliyev to attend
items.summary: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev will attend the UN climate summit COP31, held from 9 to 20 November in the city of Antalya, the first that Türkiye has hosted.
items.imageAlt: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev

items.title: Trump says he did not know his wealth grew by 3 billion dollars
items.summary: President Donald Trump told CBS News' 60 Minutes that he did not know his wealth had grown by 3 billion dollars since he returned to office, saying a son of his handles his finances.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of President Donald Trump

items.title: Pope Leo XIV, in Buenos Aires, urges Milei to safeguard democracy
items.summary: In his first speech in Buenos Aires, Pope Leo XIV called on President Javier Milei and Argentina's politicians to safeguard democracy and to use their words carefully.
items.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV waving to the crowd

items.title: Trump offers UFC chief Dana White the job of White House press secretary
items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Truth Social on Saturday that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, head of the UFC, Al Jazeera reported; White is expected to meet Trump on Monday to discuss it.
items.imageAlt: Dana White, head of the UFC

items.title: Araghchi: Mediators on Iran-US peace deal have stopped travelling
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told state television on Sunday that mediators working on a peace deal between Iran and the United States have stopped travelling since the US midterm elections, which he described as a "shock". He said it would take time before the atmosphere is right for the trips to resume.
items.imageAlt: Abbas Araghchi meeting Rafael Grossi, director of the IAEA, in Vienna

items.title: Leeds United condemn online racist abuse aimed at Jayden Bogle
items.summary: Leeds United have condemned "disgusting" online racist abuse directed at defender Jayden Bogle after Saturday's 1-0 win over Tottenham. Bogle was accused over a tackle on Mathys Tel that the referee did not punish after a VAR review, and Tottenham said they will submit a formal complaint.
items.imageAlt: Elland Road, the stadium of Leeds United, in the city of Leeds

items.title: Somalia and Libya hold talks on strengthening economic and financial cooperation
items.summary: Somalia's Foreign Minister Abdisalam Ali met Libya's Finance Minister Rashid Abu Qaffah in Tripoli, where they discussed strengthening economic and financial cooperation and increasing Somalia's live-animal exports.
items.imageAlt: Somali Foreign Minister Abdisalam Ali and Libyan Finance Minister Rashid Abu Qaffah shaking hands in Tripoli

items.title: Trump: Renewed attacks on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks make progress
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said in a phone interview with CNN on Sunday that it is "highly unlikely" the US will return to war with Iran as long as there is progress in talks on its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. He said it depends on whether Iran signs "a very strong agreement".
items.imageAlt: US President Donald Trump giving an interview, photo from 2025

items.title: South Sudan: Dispute over SPLM primaries in Greater Pibor
items.summary: A group of delegates from the ruling SPLM party has accused the committee running the primaries in the Greater Pibor administration of bias and of backing a particular candidate. The process, which had been running for nearly 2 weeks, was suspended on Friday, with officials citing "technical challenges".
items.imageAlt: A view of Pibor, South Sudan

items.title: Erdoğan joins Aliyev for Azerbaijan's Victory Day commemorations in Karabakh
items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan attended Azerbaijan's 6th Victory Day commemorations in Karabakh on Sunday at the invitation of President Ilham Aliyev. At a joint press conference, Aliyev said the unity of the two countries "will last forever".
items.imageAlt: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, photo from 2025

items.title: Russia says it hit power substations and 3 Ukraine-bound ships; hundreds of thousands without power
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said overnight strikes hit 3 cargo ships it accused of carrying weapons for Ukraine and 2 electricity substations. France 24 said hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without power on Sunday after Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.
items.imageAlt: A darkened street in Kyiv after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, November 2022

items.title: Norway: Fans injured after part of the stand gives way at Tromsø stadium
items.summary: Several fans were injured, one of whom was taken to hospital, after part of the away section at Tromsø's stadium gave way during Sunday's match against Bodø/Glimt, both clubs said. The match was stopped shortly before half-time.
items.imageAlt: Alfheim Stadium in Tromsø, Norway

items.title: Egypt: Death toll from Giza train collision rises to 4, with 88 injured
items.summary: Egypt's health ministry said at least 4 people were killed and nearly 90 injured when two trains collided in Giza province near Cairo. Earlier reports had put the number of injured at 64 with no confirmed deaths.
items.imageAlt: A train of the Egyptian National Railways (ENR)

items.title: Amsterdam: Tens of thousands march to demand Dutch government action against Israel
items.summary: Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday, pressing the Dutch government to take tougher action against Israel over Gaza.
items.imageAlt: Dam Square in central Amsterdam, with the Royal Palace and the Nieuwe Kerk

items.title: Juba: City authorities review security operations in neighbourhoods and markets
items.summary: Juba city authorities are reviewing security operations in neighbourhoods and markets, focusing on young people engaged in unlicensed brokering and on improving general order.
items.imageAlt: A market in Juba, the capital of South Sudan

items.title: England await results of Marc Guehi injury scan ahead of Nations League matches
items.summary: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi will have a scan on a hip complaint on Sunday to determine whether he can join up with England this week. The 26-year-old was substituted at half-time of City's defeat by Nottingham Forest on Saturday.
items.imageAlt: Marc Guehi in England's match against Panama at the 2026 World Cup

items.title: Poland: Terror investigation opened into Krakow shooting, two days of national mourning declared
items.summary: Poland on Sunday opened a terrorism investigation into Saturday's shooting on Krakow's Main Square in which 6 people were killed, and declared two days of national mourning. Authorities said the 24-year-old suspect was fascinated by far-right ideologies.
items.imageAlt: The Pod Złotą Głową building on the Main Market Square in Kraków's Old Town

items.title: France: Europe will take part in US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
items.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on Sunday that Europeans will be represented, and France will take part, in the US-mediated Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday.
items.imageAlt: Jean-Noël Barrot, French Minister of Foreign Affairs

items.title: Pope Leo XIV urges men to respect their wives amid femicide crisis in Latin America
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday urged men to treat their wives with respect as he wrapped up the first leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America. The region has recorded nearly 20,000 women killed because of their gender over the past five years.
items.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV on the balcony of Saint Peter's Basilica after his election in 2025

items.title: Egypt: 64 injured in train crash south of Cairo
items.summary: Two trains collided on Sunday in the al-Ayyat district of Giza province, south of Cairo, injuring 64 people, according to Egypt's Ministry of Health. The Egyptian Railway Authority said emergency teams and cranes were sent to clear the wreckage.
items.imageAlt: A train of the Egyptian National Railways (ENR) at Alexandria station

items.title: South Sudan: Political parties' election dialogue to resume on Monday to adopt resolutions
items.summary: Leaders of South Sudan's political parties have agreed to reconvene in Juba on Monday, 9 November, to finalise and adopt the resolutions of the election dialogue ahead of the general elections in December 2026, the office of the SPLM Secretary General said. The date of the closing ceremony will be set in consultation…
items.imageAlt: Dr Akol Paul Kordit, Secretary General of South Sudan's SPLM party

items.title: Lionel Messi becomes first player to win the MLS Golden Boot in two consecutive seasons
items.summary: Inter Miami's Lionel Messi scored 26 goals in 31 games, becoming the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The 39-year-old Messi also provided 17 assists.
items.imageAlt: Lionel Messi playing for Inter Miami (2025)

items.title: Museveni urges Italian investors to invest in industrialisation in Uganda
items.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni met a delegation of more than 80 people from Italy in Entebbe and urged them to invest in coffee and lithium battery industries. Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja said Italy has allocated 120 million euros to Uganda's coffee sector, and a development cooperation agreement was signed at…
items.imageAlt: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni

items.title: US forms task force to block Iran's land supply routes
