items.summary: US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it has created a new task force, Task Force Iron Gate, aimed at stopping weapons and sanctioned goods moving across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM also said 147 commercial vessels have been redirected since July, while Iranian media reported explosions on Qeshm…
items.imageAlt: The Strait of Hormuz seen from near Bandar Abbas, Iran

items.title: Canary island of El Hierro declares emergency after rise in migrant arrivals
items.summary: Authorities on the Spanish island of El Hierro declared an emergency and asked the government in Madrid for help after more than 3,300 migrants arrived on about 30 boats since the start of November, local officials said. The island has about 11,400 residents.
items.imageAlt: The coastal village of La Restinga, on the island of El Hierro

items.title: La Liga: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 at the Mestalla
items.summary: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 at the Mestalla on Saturday, with goals from Federico Valverde, Arda Güler and Kylian Mbappé, Yahoo Sports reported, a result also confirmed by VAVEL. The win, their eighth in a row, put Real Madrid level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona.
items.imageAlt: The Mestalla stadium in Valencia

items.title: Israel's president picks Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form the next government
items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, with forming the next government after 67 lawmakers backed him while Netanyahu received 46. Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14 days, to secure at least 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats.
items.imageAlt: Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party

items.title: France: more than 140,000 people protest against the rising cost of living
items.summary: France's Interior Ministry said about 146,000 people, 46,000 of them in Paris, protested nationwide on Saturday against the rising cost of living, while unions put the figure at 250,000. Police used tear gas in Paris and Lyon, in the fourth consecutive weekend of protests.
items.imageAlt: An earlier demonstration in the streets of Paris (2023)

items.title: Tennis: Carlos Alcaraz beats Casper Ruud, will face Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Casper Ruud 6-4, 6-4 in the Paris Masters semi-finals, while Ben Shelton beat Luca Van Assche 5-7, 6-3, 6-4, ESPN reported, results also confirmed by the ATP Tour. Alcaraz said he wants revenge against Shelton after losing their last meeting at the US Open.
items.imageAlt: Carlos Alcaraz playing at Roland Garros 2025

items.title: US offers a reward of up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear programme
items.summary: The US State Department's Rewards for Justice programme announced a reward of up to $20 million, and possible relocation, for anyone providing information about Iran's nuclear programme. Iran insists its programme is peaceful and that it does not seek a nuclear weapon.
items.imageAlt: The US State Department building in Washington

items.title: Pope Leo XIV holds his first mass in Uruguay during Latin America tour
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated mass on Saturday in the city of Paysandu in western Uruguay, attended by about 40,000 people according to the Vatican, as part of a 12-day tour of Latin America. The visit comes after lung surgery last month, and he travels to Argentina on Sunday.
items.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV (May 2025)

items.title: Arsenal beat Hull City 1-0 with a late goal from Martin Ødegaard
items.summary: Arsenal beat Hull City 1-0 in the Premier League at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with captain Martin Ødegaard scoring in the 72nd minute after following up a shot from Noni Madueke.
items.imageAlt: Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in London

items.title: All Blacks beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield
items.summary: New Zealand's rugby team beat Scotland 43-21 in Edinburgh on Saturday in the Nations Championship, scoring seven tries to Scotland's three, BBC Sport and the official All Blacks website reported. Scotland, only three points behind at half-time, failed to score in the second half.
items.imageAlt: Murrayfield Stadium in Edinburgh

items.title: Poland: At least 6 people killed in a shooting on Krakow's main market square
items.summary: Krakow police said an armed man driving a car opened fire on Saturday on people in the city's main market square, killing at least 6 people and wounding 15 others. Police said the suspect was shot and injured and taken to hospital.
items.imageAlt: Krakow's Main Market Square (Rynek Główny) and St. Mary's Basilica

items.title: F1: Hamilton and Verstappen to start from the back at the São Paulo Grand Prix
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) and Max Verstappen (Red Bull) will start Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix from the back of the grid after their cars were fitted with complete new power units. Charles Leclerc received a 10-place penalty and George Russell 5 places.
items.imageAlt: The start-finish straight at the Interlagos circuit in São Paulo, Brazil

items.title: New Zealand election produces no clear winner after a very tight result
items.summary: Preliminary results from Saturday's election show Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party won 42 seats, 19 short of the number needed, while Chris Hipkins' Labour Party won 36. Both sides are preparing for coalition talks that could take weeks.
items.imageAlt: New Zealand's parliament buildings in Wellington

items.title: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff
items.summary: President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller, the deputy chief of staff and architect of his tough immigration policy, to replace Susie Wiles, after the Republican Party's historic losses in the midterm elections.
items.imageAlt: Stephen Miller aboard Air Force One, 2017

items.title: Kenya: Sugar production up 56.7% as prices fall
items.summary: Data from the Kenya Sugar Board show that local factories produced 690,521 tonnes of sugar between January and September 2026, compared with 440,652 tonnes in the same period last year. The average retail price fell to Sh155 per kilo in September 2026, from Sh171 in September 2025.
items.imageAlt: A tractor hauling sugarcane in Migori, Kenya

items.title: UK warns its citizens against travel to Moyale after violence on the Ethiopian border
items.summary: The UK Foreign Office (FCDO) on 6 November advised its citizens against all but essential travel to the town of Moyale and the 5 kilometres around it on the Kenya-Ethiopia border, citing violence in Ethiopia that has affected the Kenyan side. Kenya's Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja made a security visit to…
items.imageAlt: The road to Moyale on the Kenya-Ethiopia border

items.title: Wau: State authorities close the offices of two airlines over a $5 tax dispute
items.summary: The authorities of South Sudan's Western Bahr el Ghazal state have closed the offices of Kush Airlines and Arojet Airlines in the town of Wau after they refused to collect a 5-dollar ticket tax from passengers. State officials said the tax is lawful and is paid by passengers, not by the airlines.
items.imageAlt: A cargo plane landing at Wau airport, South Sudan

items.title: Kenya: McDonald Mariga removed as FKF vice-president
items.summary: At a special general meeting of the Football Kenya Federation (FKF) in Meru on Saturday, 65 delegates voted to remove vice-president McDonald Mariga, the former Inter Milan star, and 6 other members of the National Executive Committee. AFC Leopards chairman Boniface Ambani was the only one to oppose it.
items.imageAlt: McDonald Mariga during training

items.title: Kenya: Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years in prison over the Shakahola killings
items.summary: A court in Kenya on Friday sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison after he was found guilty over the deaths of 190 children who were starved and killed in the Shakahola forest. Justice Diana Kavedza said the sentence consists of 100 years for killing by starvation and 100 years for direct killing.
items.imageAlt: The Galana River near Shakahola, Kilifi county, Kenya

items.title: Tanzania secures $1.2 billion to build the Tabora–Kigoma section of the SGR railway
items.summary: Tanzania has secured financing of 1.2 billion dollars arranged by the African Development Bank (AfDB) to build the 411-kilometre Tabora–Kigoma section of the SGR railway. The agreement, which involves 9 banks, is part of a 2.3 billion dollar financing package and includes an 800 million dollar guarantee provided by…
items.imageAlt: Passengers leaving an SGR train in Tanzania

items.title: Cricket: Usman Khawaja says the whole Australia team knew about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal
items.summary: Former Australia player Usman Khawaja told The Sydney Morning Herald that the whole squad knew about the 2018 ball-tampering plan known as 'Sandpapergate'. Cricket Australia said it remains comfortable with the findings of its original investigation but will consider any new evidence.
items.imageAlt: Usman Khawaja during the 2019 Ashes

items.title: Somalia at a dangerous crossroads: will it learn the lessons of Libya and Sudan?
items.summary: Somalia's political disputes, particularly over the Constitution, elections and the struggle for power, could endanger the country's stability. There are fears that foreign countries could exploit internal divisions, as happened in Libya and Sudan. Somalis are urged to resolve their political differences and to…
items.imageAlt: A man in a blue suit and glasses, official photo.

items.title: Europa League: Kamada's late goal earns Crystal Palace a 1-1 draw with Hoffenheim
items.summary: Crystal Palace drew 1-1 with Hoffenheim after Daichi Kamada scored in the 90+1st minute, with Alexander Prass having given Hoffenheim the lead in the 7th minute, Bundesliga.com reported. In Thursday's other games, Milan lost 0-2 at home to Ferencváros, while Bournemouth won 1-3 at Sparta Praha, according to UEFA's…
items.imageAlt: Japanese player Daichi Kamada

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a missile fired towards the Medina region
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Yemen's Houthis towards the Medina region, after the civil defence agency warned of danger near the port of Yanbu. The Houthis denied targeting the city, calling the accusation a fabrication.
items.imageAlt: General view of the city of Medina in Saudi Arabia

items.title: George Russell vows a deep look in the mirror after a disappointing season
items.summary: Mercedes driver George Russell said he will take a deep look at himself to work out how he can improve after a 2026 season he called disappointing. Russell has won only 3 races, while his teammate Kimi Antonelli has won 9 on his way to becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history.
items.imageAlt: Mercedes driver George Russell at the 2025 Italian Grand Prix

items.title: California Governor Newsom commutes death sentences of 548 prisoners to life in prison
items.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state to life in prison. The decision is seen as largely symbolic, as California has not executed anyone since 2006, and it comes as Newsom is discussed as a possible candidate.
items.imageAlt: California Governor Gavin Newsom

items.title: Iran says several oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said at least 5 oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said one of the vessels struck a mine, as the US and Israeli war on Iran remains unresolved.
items.imageAlt: Photo taken from space showing the Strait of Hormuz

items.title: Eritrea: President Isaias Afwerki meets China's special envoy for the Horn of Africa
items.summary: President Isaias Afwerki met Hu Changchun, China's Special Envoy for Horn of Africa Affairs, in Asmara on 5 November, and they discussed bilateral ties and the situation in the region, Eritrea's Ministry of Information said. Hu reiterated China's position that Eritrea's sovereignty and territorial integrity must be…
items.imageAlt: Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki

items.title: Uganda prepares to distribute free fertiliser to smallholder coffee farmers
items.summary: Uganda's government is preparing to distribute free fertiliser to smallholder coffee farmers in selected districts to raise production. The paper said more than 27 truckloads of fertiliser have been offloaded in Entebbe, and that Intracom Fertilizers has been contracted to supply organic fertiliser for coffee, cocoa…
items.imageAlt: Farmers harvesting coffee cherries

items.title: Tech and AI shares fall after the US election
items.summary: US stock markets fell on Thursday, with the Nasdaq down 4.8 percent, the S&P 500 down 3.6 percent and the Dow Jones down 2.8 percent by midday. The BBC said SpaceX shares fell more than 9 percent and Tesla more than 11 percent, as investors worry about possible curbs on data centres and the AI industry.
items.imageAlt: The New York Stock Exchange building on Wall Street

items.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña resigns after the collapse of ueno bank
items.summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday after the collapse of digital lender ueno left millions of customers unable to access their accounts and the opposition began impeachment proceedings. Peña said he took the decision for the country's stability and to preserve democratic institutions, while Vice…
items.imageAlt: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña

items.title: Ethiopia and China sign $15 million grant for the Ethiopia–Djibouti railway
items.summary: The governments of Ethiopia and China have signed a $15 million grant agreement in Addis Ababa to strengthen the operation and maintenance of the Ethiopia–Djibouti railway. It was signed by State Minister of Finance Tiguist Fisseha and Liu Xiaoguang of the Chinese embassy, and covers spare parts for electric…
items.imageAlt: A train of Ethiopian Railways on the line

items.title: Kenya: Malindi court suspends recruitment of IEBC chief executive
items.summary: The Employment and Labour Relations Court in Malindi has temporarily suspended the recruitment of the Secretary and Chief Executive Officer of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), halting interviews scheduled for 12 and 13 November. The order by Justice J.N. Abuodha stems from a petition filed…
items.imageAlt: Logo of Kenya's Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)

items.title: Japanese football official Kozo Tashima to stand against Infantino for FIFA president
items.summary: Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association, announced on Thursday that he will challenge Gianni Infantino in FIFA's presidential election in March. Tashima, 68, a former member of the FIFA Council, is the second person to declare a candidacy, after former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega.
items.imageAlt: FIFA headquarters in Zurich

items.title: Armenia plans to apply for EU membership in 2027 or 2028
items.summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on Thursday that his country would formally submit an application for full European Union membership in 2027 or 2028. The statement comes as relations between Armenia and its longtime ally Russia continue to deteriorate.
items.imageAlt: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan addressing the European Parliament in Strasbourg in 2023

items.title: Hakimi, Mané, Semenyo and Díaz among CAF Awards 2026 nominees
items.summary: Defending winner Achraf Hakimi, Sadio Mané, Antoine Semenyo and Brahim Díaz are on the men's shortlist for the CAF Awards 2026. The awards will be presented on the 7th of next month in Lagos, Nigeria.
items.imageAlt: Achraf Hakimi playing for Morocco in their match against Norway on 7 June 2026

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal's national team
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, has announced his retirement from Portugal's national team after playing 234 matches and scoring 146 goals since 2003, both world records. In a video posted on Instagram, Ronaldo said the day had come for him to hand back the number 7 shirt.
items.imageAlt: Cristiano Ronaldo in a Portugal shirt during a friendly between Portugal and Argentina in Geneva

items.title: Saudi Arabia and Syria sign a defence cooperation agreement
items.summary: Saudi Arabia and Syria signed a defence cooperation agreement on Wednesday during a visit to Riyadh by Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, the Saudi state news agency SPA reported, as cited by Daily Sabah. Al-Sharaa met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; details of the agreement were not disclosed.
items.imageAlt: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa with President Donald Trump during his visit to Saudi Arabia in 2025

items.title: National strikes and protests take place in France
items.summary: Five trade unions joined a national day of strikes and protests in France, demanding higher wages and protection of public services. Authorities expected 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators, while Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 70,000 police and gendarmes had been deployed.
items.imageAlt: A workers' demonstration in Paris in January 2020 against the pension reform

items.title: Kenya: Pharmacy Board warns against misuse of cetirizine tablets
items.summary: Kenya's Pharmacy and Poisons Board (PPB) has warned the public against using cetirizine tablets for an unintended purpose being promoted on social media, saying there is no scientific evidence to support it. The board noted that cetirizine is an oral allergy medicine, to be taken as directed by a health professional.
items.imageAlt: Cetirizine tablets, an oral allergy medicine

items.title: Alan Jones, 1980 Formula 1 champion, dies aged 80
items.summary: Alan Jones, the last Australian and the first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world championship, has died aged 80. His wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released by Motorsport Australia that he died on 5 November after a short illness; Jones won 12 Grands Prix.
items.imageAlt: The Williams FW07B in which Alan Jones won the 1980 Formula 1 championship

items.title: Tanzania: High Court to rule on 6 November in Tundu Lissu's case
items.summary: Tanzania's High Court, Dar es Salaam Sub-Registry, will deliver its judgment on 6 November in the treason trial of opposition Chadema party chairman Tundu Lissu. A three-judge bench led by Justice Dunstan Ndunguru will decide whether to convict or acquit him.
items.imageAlt: Tundu Lissu addressing the Tanzanian parliament in Dodoma

items.title: Melania Trump to host Ukrainian and Russian officials at the White House
items.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump will host officials from Moscow and Kyiv at the White House on Thursday, ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the war in Ukraine. The TASS news agency, citing Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, said Kirill Dmitriev and Yana Lantratova would meet her if arrangements allowed, while…
items.imageAlt: Official White House portrait of First Lady Melania Trump, 2025

items.title: CERN scientists find evidence of an extremely rare particle transformation
items.summary: Using the Large Hadron Collider, CERN scientists have found evidence of an extremely rare process in which a so-called 'beauty particle' transforms into other particles, something predicted to happen just once in every 10 billion cases. Researchers said this offers a way to explore what they call the 'zeptoverse'.
items.imageAlt: The Large Hadron Collider tunnel at CERN

items.title: UN warns against South Sudan including Abyei in its elections
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in a report to the Security Council that South Sudan's plan to include the disputed Abyei region in its December 2026 general elections could heighten tensions with Sudan. Sudan formally protested the decision on 13 July, saying it violates agreements between the two…
items.imageAlt: A general view of the town of Abyei

items.title: Como beat Lens 9-1 to equal the Champions League record
items.summary: Como, coached by Cesc Fàbregas, won 9-1 at Lens, with Anastasios Douvikas scoring three goals. The nine goals equal the most scored by one team in a Champions League match, after Bayern Munich's 9-2 win over Dinamo Zagreb in 2024.
items.imageAlt: The Stade Bollaert-Delelis stadium in the city of Lens

items.title: UN: Gunfire damages tents of displaced people in Rafah
items.summary: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said gunfire hit and damaged several tents at a displacement site in northern Rafah, Gaza, injuring people. Secretary-General's spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said civilians and humanitarian workers must be protected.
items.imageAlt: An aerial view of tents of displaced Palestinians in the Al-Mawasi area of the Gaza Strip

items.title: Champions League: Real Madrid beat AEK 3-2, Liverpool lose 3-2 to Fenerbahce
items.summary: Real Madrid won 3-2 at AEK Athens after a stoppage-time goal by Federico Valverde, with Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé also scoring, according to Real Madrid's official website. Liverpool lost 3-2 in Istanbul, with Muriqi scoring Fenerbahce's winner, as confirmed by Liverpool's website.
items.imageAlt: Federico Valverde playing in a Real Madrid shirt

items.title: UNCTAD: Developing countries bear the heaviest burden of fuel prices
items.summary: A new UNCTAD report says developing countries have borne the heaviest burden of rising fuel prices after the war closed the Strait of Hormuz in February. For example, diesel in Nigeria rose about 83% between late February and the end of August, while in Ireland it rose 9%.
items.imageAlt: A fuel pump at a filling station

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh removes the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
items.summary: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has removed Supreme Court Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed and appointed Ibrahim Idle Suleiman in his place, according to a statement from the presidency reported by Dawan Africa. The presidency said the decision was based on complaints from judges and legal professionals, while Somali…
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud speaking to the press

items.title: Drone attacks kill three people in Russia's Belgorod region
items.summary: Local Russian authorities said Ukrainian drone attacks killed three people in the Belgorod region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia's overnight attacks damaged power facilities and energy substations in nine regions, causing power outages.
items.imageAlt: An aerial view of the Russian city of Belgorod

items.title: Trump: The Iran war affected the election, but I did the right thing
items.summary: President Donald Trump admitted that the attack on Iran and high fuel prices contributed to the Republican Party's midterm losses, but told the Wall Street Journal: "I did the right thing," Al Jazeera reported. Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that the reason for the defeat was the war.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of US Vice President JD Vance

items.title: Somalia approves six-month plan to reach unvaccinated children
items.summary: The National Committee on Immunisation and Polio Eradication, chaired by Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre, approved a six-month plan to expand child vaccination. According to WHO and UNICEF, up to 1.5 million Somali children under five have never received routine vaccination.
items.imageAlt: A Somali boy receiving the polio vaccine at a hospital in Mogadishu

items.title: International Ice Hockey Federation still opposes decision to reinstate Russia
items.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said it still disagrees with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision that lifted Russia's ban, warning of challenges related to visas and security. Norway, Denmark, Sweden and the Czech Republic said their teams will not play Russia at next year's World…
items.imageAlt: An ice hockey match between Sweden and Switzerland at the 2019 IIHF World Championship

items.title: Rory McIlroy backs letting former LIV players return to the DP World Tour
items.summary: Golf star Rory McIlroy backed the DP World Tour's decision to allow former LIV Golf players such as Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia back in 2027. McIlroy said LIV turned professional golf into an 'arms race' and called for sustainable business practices.
items.imageAlt: Golfer Rory McIlroy

items.title: Democratic Party takes control of both chambers of the US Congress
items.summary: Democrats retook the House of Representatives and gained at least six seats in the Senate, giving them control of the whole of Congress. President Donald Trump said he was not on the ballot, while Hakeem Jeffries described the result as the beginning of America's comeback.
items.imageAlt: The US Capitol building in Washington

items.title: Abdul El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim senator in the United States
items.summary: Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers for the Senate seat in Michigan and will become the country's first Muslim senator. El-Sayed, 42, whose parents emigrated from Egypt, said his campaign showed that 'the many can win' over money.
items.imageAlt: Abdul El-Sayed testifying at a US Senate committee hearing

items.title: Spain's transport minister resigns after train crash that killed 69 people
items.summary: Minister Óscar Puente resigned less than a week after the train crash on the Madrid-Seville line, saying a minister cannot stay in office after two serious accidents within a year. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced an aid package worth €30 million.
items.imageAlt: Photo of Óscar Puente, Spain's transport minister

items.title: South Africa votes in local council elections seen as a test for the ANC
items.summary: The electoral commission IEC said a record 29.2 million people registered to vote in the municipal council elections, seen as a test for the ANC. President Cyril Ramaphosa wrote that failures in local government have reduced public trust; final results are expected on Sunday.
items.imageAlt: Voters queueing at a polling station in South Africa

items.title: Former baseball star Mark Teixeira wins a seat in the US House of Representatives
items.summary: Mark Teixeira, a three-time MLB All-Star, won the seat for Texas's 21st district for the Republican Party, defeating Democrat Kristin Hook. The seat was previously held by Chip Roy, who did not run again.
items.imageAlt: Mark Teixeira in a New York Yankees uniform

items.title: Somali government rejects ambassador Israel appointed to Hargeisa and planned embassy
items.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation said the appointment of the ambassador and the laying of the foundation stone for an Israeli embassy in Hargeisa did not receive the federal government's approval and have no legal effect. The ministry said it would take diplomatic, political and legal…
items.imageAlt: General view of the city of Hargeisa

items.title: Jon Ossoff wins re-election to his Senate seat in Georgia
items.summary: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff defeated Republican candidate Mike Collins in the US midterm elections. With 56% of votes counted, Ossoff had 63% and Collins 29%; which party will control the two chambers of Congress has not yet been announced.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of Senator Jon Ossoff

items.title: Puntland House of Representatives questions Education Ministry leaders
items.summary: The Puntland House of Representatives, chaired by Speaker Abdirizak Ahmed Said, heard a report from the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, after which MPs questioned officials about the ministry's performance and education services.
items.imageAlt: A session of the Puntland House of Representatives in Garowe

items.title: Ilhan Omar elected to the US House of Representatives for a fifth time
items.summary: Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar has been re-elected to the seat for Minnesota's 5th district, which she has represented since 2019. In her victory speech she thanked her supporters, most of whom are Somali.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of Representative Ilhan Omar

items.title: Somalia and Turkey discuss strengthening military and security cooperation
items.summary: Defence Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi met in Mogadishu with General Sabahattin Kılınç of the Turkish Armed Forces' general command, and they discussed defence cooperation, security in the Horn of Africa and the fight against Al-Shabaab. Fiqi praised Turkey's support for training and equipping the Somali forces.
items.imageAlt: Somali soldiers undergoing military training in Turkey

items.title: Government: Uganda's troop withdrawal does not mean all its forces are leaving
items.summary: National Security Adviser Ambassador Aweys Haji Yusuf Ahmed said the troops leaving are those deployed under a bilateral agreement, while Ugandan forces in AUSSOM will remain. The UPDF had earlier said all its forces in Somalia will leave by the end of 2027.
items.imageAlt: A vehicle of Ugandan African Union troops on patrol in the town of Qoryooley

items.title: King Charles expresses deep sorrow over the slave trade but offers no apology
items.summary: Britain's King Charles III said at the opening of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda, that the transatlantic slave trade filled him with horror and deep personal sorrow. He did not offer a formal apology, while Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali said an apology…
items.imageAlt: Britain's King Charles III

items.title: Greenland's parliament approves security deal with the US and Denmark
items.summary: Greenland's parliament approved the agreement on Tuesday by 16 votes in favour and 0 against, with 7 lawmakers abstaining. The deal allows the US to expand its activities at Pituffik Space Base and will take effect once Denmark and Greenland complete the required parliamentary processes.
items.imageAlt: Pituffik Space Base (Thule Air Base) in northern Greenland seen from the air

items.title: Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0, PSG thrash Villarreal 6-0
items.summary: Lamine Yamal (minute 7) and a Raphinha double (52 and 64) gave Barcelona the Champions League win. Other results that night, confirmed by UEFA's official website, include Manchester United 3-2 Roma, Villarreal 0-6 Paris Saint-Germain and Atlético de Madrid 0-2 Bayern München.
items.imageAlt: Barcelona player Raphinha wearing the Brazil national team shirt

items.title: Zelensky hopes Abu Dhabi talks will lead to a meeting with Putin
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, meeting Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, said he hopes the Abu Dhabi talks on 10 and 11 November will open the way to a three-way meeting at leaders' level. US special envoy Steve Witkoff announced the talks, while the Kremlin said the Russian delegation will be led by…
items.imageAlt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky

items.title: National Salvation Forum agrees to talks with President Hassan Sheikh
items.summary: The opposition said it is giving the president a final opportunity to resolve the dispute over the elections and the constitution, and it named a 3-member committee that will meet the government's technical committee on the 14th of this month. It was reported that it is not yet known whether Puntland and Jubaland will…
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud speaking at the National Leaders Forum, Mogadishu 2016

items.title: At least 73 injured in Russian strike on a hospital in Kharkiv
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia attacked a hospital and power facilities in many Ukrainian regions overnight, using 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles. Russia's Defence Ministry said it targeted power facilities that supply Ukraine's army and military factories.
items.imageAlt: The university building on Freedom Square in Kharkiv

items.title: Voting begins in the US midterm elections
items.summary: It was reported that the vote will decide all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats and governorships in 36 states, and is seen as a test for President Donald Trump. The Department of Justice said it has deployed 1,000 election monitors across all 50 states.
items.imageAlt: A sign pointing to a polling place in the United States

items.title: Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel dies after an on-field collision
items.summary: Tenerife announced on Tuesday the death of its 30-year-old forward, who was injured in a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono in Monday's La Liga 2 match. The game, at 2-2, was abandoned and Owono was shown a red card; the news was confirmed by Al Jazeera and ESPN.
items.imageAlt: Tenerife's Heliodoro Rodríguez López stadium in Santa Cruz de Tenerife

items.title: Ugandan troops hand over security of Barawe and Shalanbood to the Somali National Army
items.summary: Somali Guardian said the handover ended more than a decade of Ugandan military presence in the two towns in the Lower Shabelle region. Ugandan military spokesman Colonel Chris Magezi said all Ugandan forces in Somalia, including those serving with AUSSOM, will leave in phases by the end of 2027.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan AMISOM soldiers walking through the town of Barawe in 2014

items.title: Cyclone Murasu hits India's eastern coast
items.summary: The India Meteorological Department said the cyclone made landfall near the town of Ongole in Andhra Pradesh state, the second cyclone to hit the area within a week. Officials said no deaths had been reported so far, and plans were in place to evacuate up to 30,000 people from danger zones.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the town of Ongole in Andhra Pradesh state

items.title: India v Pakistan draws more ticket requests than the final at the 2027 Cricket World Cup
items.summary: The International Cricket Council (ICC) said the match between the two countries on 10 October at the Wanderers ground in Johannesburg has drawn 8.4 million ticket requests, while the final received nearly 8 million. The tournament will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
items.imageAlt: The Wanderers cricket ground in Johannesburg

items.title: FIFA to show council members documents on the World Cup stake sale plan
items.summary: Al Jazeera, citing British media, reported that the 37 members of the FIFA Council can view the documents only by in-person appointment in Zurich, and the information will not be released to the public. Gianni Infantino's $4.2bn plan was dropped in July after a global backlash, and UEFA had demanded its details.
items.imageAlt: FIFA headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland

items.title: Luka Dončić scores 42 points as the Lakers beat the Miami Heat 138-117
items.summary: Dončić also had 13 assists, and it was the fourth time in his last 5 games that he scored more than 40 points. The win took the Lakers to 6-2 this season, a result also reported by US News.
items.imageAlt: Luka Dončić wearing the Lakers number 77 jersey

items.title: Two helicopters collide near Everest, killing one person
items.summary: Nepali authorities said a 47-year-old Indian man died, while a New Zealand national and a Nepali pilot were injured. The crash happened in Pheriche village at about 4,200 metres, as both aircraft were trying to land below Everest base camp.
items.imageAlt: Pheriche village and the Khumbu valley in the Everest region, Nepal

items.title: Australia's High Court hears challenge to children's social media ban
items.summary: Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project group asked the court to strike down the law banning children under 16 from using social media, which took effect last December. The Australian government says the restrictions protect children from graphic content and online predators.
items.imageAlt: The High Court of Australia building in Canberra

items.title: Saudi Arabia's 2027 Asian Cup moved to December
items.summary: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said the 24-team tournament will now run from 23 December 2027 to 21 January 2028, instead of opening on 7 January 2027, because of logistical and travel difficulties caused by the regional situation. The new dates will be submitted to FIFA for approval.
items.imageAlt: King Fahd International Stadium in Riyadh

items.title: Cyberattack hits supermarket refrigeration in several European countries
items.summary: A cyberattack on refrigeration control systems affected large supermarkets in Belgium, Sweden, Finland, Ireland and other countries, forcing large amounts of food to be thrown away. Belgium has opened a criminal investigation, and no one has been officially named as responsible.
items.imageAlt: Dairy refrigerator in a supermarket (illustrative photo, Norway 2017)

items.title: Puntland parliament holds consultation with politicians on constitutional amendments
items.summary: Puntland House of Representatives Speaker Abdirisaq Ahmed Siciid opened a consultative meeting of a special committee reviewing proposed amendments to Puntland's constitution. Former officials who served in Puntland and the federal government attended and presented their views and recommendations.
items.imageAlt: Abdirisaq Ahmed Siciid, Speaker of the Puntland House of Representatives

items.title: NBA: Gilgeous-Alexander scores 43 as Thunder beat Cavaliers 117-112
items.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 43 points, his season high, to lead the Oklahoma City Thunder to a win over the Cleveland Cavaliers. Donovan Mitchell had 17 points and 11 assists for the Cavaliers, GMA News and TSN reported.
items.imageAlt: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander playing for the Oklahoma City Thunder (2022)

items.title: Everton beat Newcastle 1-0 at St James' Park
items.summary: Thierno Barry scored the only goal of the game in minute 49, while Newcastle's Jacob Ramsey was sent off in stoppage time after two yellow cards. The result was confirmed by ESPN and beIN SPORTS.
items.imageAlt: St James' Park stadium in Newcastle

items.title: Arab League condemns Israel's ambassador to Somaliland and the Hargeisa embassy
items.summary: The Secretary-General of the Arab League, Nabil Fahmy, said these steps have no legitimacy and violate Somalia's sovereignty and unity. The League reiterated that it rejects any official or unofficial relations with the Somaliland administration.
items.imageAlt: Headquarters of the Arab League in Cairo

items.title: US to suspend South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA duty-free trade
items.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced that South Africa and Rwanda will be suspended from the AGOA programme from 1 January 2027, saying both countries failed to meet its criteria. South Africa exported goods worth about $1.7 billion under the programme in 2025.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer (2025)

items.title: Iran says its ceasefire plan with the US can be accelerated
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the ceasefire plan Iran proposed to the US can now be implemented in two days instead of seven, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran insisted that the US lift its naval blockade and sanctions.
items.imageAlt: Abbas Araghchi, now Iran's foreign minister, on a visit to the IAEA (2021)

items.title: Germany: IG Metall union launches strikes over pay
items.summary: The IG Metall union launched strikes at companies including Audi and Mercedes-Benz, demanding a 5% pay rise for about 3.7 million workers. The union rejected the employers' offer, calling it a real-terms pay cut.
items.imageAlt: IG Metall union members on a warning strike in Witten, Germany (2012)

items.title: India says it freed the fishing vessel Azini, hijacked off the coast of Bari
items.summary: The Indian government said its navy and air force freed the Iranian-flagged fishing vessel Azini and the 20 crew members on board in a 48-hour operation in the Indian Ocean. The vessel was reportedly hijacked on 29 October between Bandar Beyla and Hafun.
items.imageAlt: Indian Navy warship INS Betwa docked at the port of Mumbai (2009)

items.title: Ukraine: 24 killed in strike on aid centre in Zaporizhzhia region
items.summary: Ukraine's emergency services said 24 people were killed in a bombing blamed on Russia that hit a school used as an aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha. President Zelenskyy condemned the attack, while Russia has previously denied targeting civilians.
items.imageAlt: Music school building in the village of Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region (2025)

items.title: France: high school students' protests resume, but on a small scale
items.summary: French high school students resumed their protests after a two-week holiday, but the Education Ministry said only 41 schools were blockaded on Monday, compared with hundreds in previous weeks.
items.imageAlt: Students blockading the Lycée Buffon in Paris, December 2024

items.title: Abdullah Öcalan moved to a new section of the İmralı island prison
items.summary: Turkey has moved Abdullah Öcalan, the jailed founder of the PKK, to a newly built section of the İmralı island prison, according to lawmakers from the DEM party.
items.imageAlt: İmralı island seen from an aircraft

items.title: Brooklyn court begins trial of two MLB players accused in a betting case
items.summary: Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, who formerly played for the Cleveland Guardians, face a trial in a federal court in Brooklyn in which prosecutors accuse them of taking money from two gamblers; both have pleaded not guilty.
items.imageAlt: The federal courthouse in Brooklyn, New York

items.title: Chinese state TV keeps blacking out Real Madrid matches after the Mbappé row
items.summary: Neither of CCTV's two sports channels showed Real Madrid's 3-0 win over Racing Santander on Sunday, as the row over a video in which Kylian Mbappé spoke about Mao Zedong continues.
items.imageAlt: Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu stadium

items.title: Bangladesh: garment workers' protests continue for a third day
items.summary: Hundreds of garment factories in Bangladesh have been disrupted as workers protest low pay and the rising cost of living.
items.imageAlt: Women working in a garment factory in Bangladesh

items.title: Hebron governor says Israeli forces have left the city after a 10-day siege
items.summary: Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said on Monday that Israeli forces had withdrawn from the West Bank city after a 10-day siege and that Palestinian security forces had taken control of the area.
items.imageAlt: The Old City of Hebron

items.title: NBA: Yaxel Lendeborg scores 37 as the Warriors beat the Clippers 124-112
items.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored 37 points, the most by a Warriors rookie since Stephen Curry in 2010.
items.imageAlt: Yaxel Lendeborg playing for Michigan, February 2026

items.title: Puntland registers troops to be trained by the United States at a base in Bosaso
items.summary: The Puntland administration has begun registering nearly 100 soldiers from various security units, whom the United States will train at a military base in Bosaso, Garowe Online said, citing local media.
items.imageAlt: General view of the city of Bosaso

items.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history
items.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, 20, finished 3rd at the Mexico City Grand Prix to win the drivers' championship, while Max Verstappen won the race, the FIA said.
items.imageAlt: Kimi Antonelli celebrating after the Chinese Grand Prix (2026)

items.title: Serie A: Juventus beat Napoli 2-0, Lazio go top
items.summary: Juventus beat 10-man Napoli 2-0, while Lazio, who beat Cagliari 2-1, went top of Serie A for the first time in 16 years.
items.imageAlt: Juventus's stadium (Allianz Stadium) in Turin, Italy

items.title: Arab Parliament condemns attack on Qatari gas tanker
items.summary: The Arab Parliament strongly condemned the targeting of Qatar's liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier Al Mayeda as it sailed in the Arabian Gulf, warning that such attacks threaten regional security and energy supplies.
items.imageAlt: The LNG carrier Mozah, owned by Qatar's Nakilat, at Ras Laffan (2010)

items.title: Erdogan Hospital in Mogadishu brings in modern equipment for detecting cancer
items.summary: The Recep Tayyip Erdogan (Digfer) Hospital in Mogadishu has added to its tissue examination department three machines brought to Somalia for the first time, the head of the department, Dr. Ismail Mohamud Abdullahi, told Dawan Africa.
items.imageAlt: The Recep Tayyip Erdogan Hospital in Mogadishu (2015)

items.title: Premier League: Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0 and go top
items.summary: A 16th-minute goal from Kai Havertz gave Arsenal their first win at Anfield in 14 years and moved them to the top of the Premier League.
items.imageAlt: Liverpool's Anfield stadium seen from the main stand

items.title: Bundesliga: Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hamburger SV 3-1
items.summary: Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hamburger SV 3-1 and climbed to 8th place in the Bundesliga, Bulinews and IANS reported.
items.imageAlt: An Eintracht Frankfurt match at its Waldstadion (Deutsche Bank Park), 2024

items.title: LaLiga: Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0
items.summary: Real Madrid scored three first-half goals away at Racing Santander to record a sixth straight win, according to reports from the club and ESPN.
items.imageAlt: El Sardinero stadium in Santander, Spain

items.title: SomBank and IBS Bank offer Islamic financing to Somali fishers
items.summary: SomBank says it has provided Somali fishers with Islamic financing of up to $2 million, while IBS Bank has unveiled a new service called “Kalluun Kaabe”.
items.imageAlt: Two Somali fishermen in the town of Barawe

items.title: Saudi Noor programme launches free eye treatment and surgery in Mogadishu
items.summary: The Saudi Noor 2026 humanitarian programme has launched free eye-care services at Madina Hospital in Mogadishu, expected to reach about 500 patients.
items.imageAlt: A doctor in the emergency room of Madina Hospital, Mogadishu (2014)

items.title: Ligue 1: Marseille beat Toulouse 2-0 at the Vélodrome
items.summary: Olympique de Marseille beat Toulouse 2-0 in a round 9 Ligue 1 match.
items.imageAlt: Olympique de Marseille's Vélodrome stadium

items.title: COP17 in Yerevan adopts a plan to speed up action to protect nature
items.summary: Countries attending the UN Biodiversity Conference (COP17) in the Armenian capital agreed the “Yerevan Pathway”, a plan to accelerate work on the 23 targets to be met by 2030.
items.imageAlt: Entrance of the UN Biodiversity Conference (COP17) venue in Yerevan, Armenia

items.title: Mo Ibrahim: democracy and human rights are declining in Africa
items.summary: Mo Ibrahim, founder of the Mo Ibrahim Foundation, told the AFP news agency that democracy and human rights are declining in Africa. The foundation's index showed economic progress but declines in security and public participation.
items.imageAlt: Mo Ibrahim giving a keynote speech in Uppsala, Sweden (2014)

items.title: President Irro receives the credentials of Israel's ambassador in Hargeisa
items.summary: Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Irro) received on Sunday, at the presidential palace in Hargeisa, the credentials of Michael Lotem, Israel's ambassador to Somaliland.
items.imageAlt: President Irro speaking in Hargeisa with the AFRICOM commander, Gen. Dagvin Anderson (November 2025)

items.title: UN mission in Western Sahara (MINURSO) ends after 35 years
items.summary: MINURSO's mandate expired at midnight on Saturday after the Security Council failed to agree on its future. Secretary-General António Guterres said the UN stands ready to keep supporting peace efforts.
items.imageAlt: MINURSO headquarters in Laayoune (2012)

items.title: Bosaso hosts Somalia's first beach soccer tournament
items.summary: The Puntland Football Association and the Somali Football Federation launched a beach soccer tournament in Bosaso on 30 October with 6 teams taking part, marking the first appearance of women in the event.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of Bosaso and its coastline (2024)

items.title: Somalia takes part in the opening of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
items.summary: Somalia's flag was among those presented at the opening of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which run from 31 October to 13 November. Somalia is represented by 17-year-old boxer Hassan Anwar, who competes in the 50-kilogram category.
items.imageAlt: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games torch relay event in Diamniadio

items.title: Golden State Valkyries win their first WNBA title
items.summary: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals to win their first title, in only their 2nd season.
items.imageAlt: Golden State Valkyries playing Indiana Fever (May 2026)

items.title: Lewis Hamilton takes pole for the Mexico City Grand Prix
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton took his first pole position as a Ferrari driver at the Mexico City Grand Prix, ahead of George Russell and Charles Leclerc.
items.imageAlt: Lewis Hamilton driving for Ferrari (2025)

items.title: Canelo Álvarez reclaims WBC super-middleweight title
items.summary: Mexican boxer Canelo Álvarez beat Christian Mbilli, a previously unbeaten champion, by unanimous decision in Riyadh to win back the WBC belt.
items.imageAlt: Canelo Álvarez throws a jab (file photo, 2017)

items.title: Nigeria investigates two suspected Ebola cases
items.summary: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said two people suspected of having Ebola were identified in the country’s northeast; they have been isolated and laboratory tests are under way.
items.imageAlt: The Ebola virus seen under an electron microscope

items.title: EU investigates reports that an Iranian-owned fishing vessel was hijacked off the Bari coast
items.summary: The European Union's naval operation ATALANTA is investigating reports that pirates hijacked the Iranian-owned fishing vessel Azini on 29 October near Bandarbeyla district. The Maritime Security Centre MSCIO urged merchant ships to remain vigilant.
items.imageAlt: EU badge on a warship taking part in Operation Atalanta (file photo, 2009)

items.title: Somalia and Oman discuss expanding trade and investment
items.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Jamaal Maxamed Xasan met Oman's ambassador to Somalia, Saalim bin Xabiib Al Camiri, in Mogadishu. It was reported that the meeting focused on strengthening trade between the two countries and creating new business opportunities.
items.imageAlt: Al Alam Palace in Muscat, Oman

items.title: Somalia and Russia discuss security cooperation and police training
items.summary: Internal Security Minister Cabdullaahi Sheekh Ismaaciil (Fartaag) met Igor Zubov, Russia's Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs. Zubov said his government is ready to share its knowledge and training in fighting crime.
items.imageAlt: Somali police officers in a training exercise at General Kahiye Police Academy, Mogadishu (file photo, 2014)

items.title: Federal government begins planning a 110 km road linking Buuhoodle and Tuulo-Samakaab
items.summary: It was reported that Minister Ayuub Ismaaciil of the federal government signed the road plan in the presence of MP Cabdi Qawdhan. The MP said the project is a major victory that will change the lives of local residents.
items.imageAlt: The town of Buuhoodle (file photo, 2015)

items.title: Barcelona thrash Alavés 6-1 as Lamine Yamal scores 2
items.summary: Barcelona beat Alavés 6-1 at the Spotify Camp Nou and returned to the top of La Liga.
items.imageAlt: Lamine Yamal on the pitch (2025)

items.title: Bayern and Dortmund draw 2-2 as Harry Kane misses a penalty
items.summary: Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund drew 2-2 at the Allianz Arena in the Bundesliga's Der Klassiker.
items.imageAlt: Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena (file photo)

items.title: AC Milan beat Inter 3-1 in the Milan derby
items.summary: AC Milan beat Inter 3-1 at San Siro, ending Inter's run of 9 league games without defeat.
items.imageAlt: Milan's San Siro stadium (file photo)

items.title: Washington DC and Virginia sue to block Trump’s triumphal arch
items.summary: Washington DC and the state of Virginia have asked a federal court to stop President Trump’s plan to build a triumphal arch at Memorial Circle, calling it unlawful.
items.imageAlt: The Arlington Memorial Bridge over the Potomac River, Washington, D.C.

items.title: Erdogan urges Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea attacks
items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, speaking in Istanbul alongside President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea are unacceptable, whoever carries them out.
items.imageAlt: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (2025)

items.title: Electoral commission opens registration of political organisations ahead of the 2027 elections
items.summary: Registration of political organisations will run from 1 to 22 November. Somalia is preparing for parliamentary elections in April 2027 and a presidential election in May 2027.
items.imageAlt: Logo of the National Independent Electoral Commission

items.title: President Deni rejects the 2027 election timetable and calls for an interim council
items.summary: Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni told Puntland television he does not see an election that Hassan Sheikh can organise, and called for an interim council to lead the country to elections. It was reported that the allegations he made have not been independently verified.
items.imageAlt: Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni speaking at the National Consultative Council in Mogadishu (2021)

items.title: Brighton beat Manchester City 1-0 away
items.summary: Yasin Ayari scored the only goal in the 11th minute as Brighton won at City’s ground for the first time, at the 18th attempt.
items.imageAlt: The Amex Stadium, home of Brighton, England (2013)

items.title: South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs to win the Test series
items.summary: South Africa won the 3rd Test at Newlands to take the series 2-1, after Australia, set 288 to win, were bowled out for 111.
items.imageAlt: Newlands Cricket Ground, Cape Town

items.title: Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 as United go 9 games without a win
items.summary: Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 at Stamford Bridge after Lisandro Martínez was sent off in the 63rd minute.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of Chelsea's Stamford Bridge stadium, London (2023)

items.title: Somaliland warns against abuses targeting Ethiopian residents of Borama
items.summary: Somaliland's Information Minister, Barkhad Jaamac Batuun, said abuse or intimidation of foreigners will not be tolerated. He said no one has the right to forcibly expel or attack a foreigner and that such matters will go through legal procedures.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the town of Borama (2024)

items.title: US Coast Guard adds Somalia to list of ports failing security standards
items.summary: The US Coast Guard said in a notice that Somalia's ports lack effective anti-terrorism measures. The decision, which took effect on 27 October, means additional security checks for ships bound for the United States after calling at Somali ports.
items.imageAlt: Shipping containers at the port of Mogadishu (file photo, 2015)

items.title: Achraf Hakimi scores a hat-trick as PSG beat Le Havre 5-1
items.summary: PSG beat Le Havre 5-1 on Friday, with Moroccan defender Achraf Hakimi scoring 3 goals and setting up 2 more.
items.imageAlt: Achraf Hakimi in a Morocco shirt (2024)

items.title: Somaliland bans civilians from carrying firearms
items.summary: Somaliland police chief Abdirahman Abdullahi said security forces have been ordered to confiscate weapons from people who do not hold a permit.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of Hargeisa (2022)

items.title: Mogadishu marks the 103rd anniversary of the Republic of Türkiye
items.summary: The Turkish Embassy in Mogadishu held a ceremony for the 103rd anniversary of the founding of the Republic of Türkiye. Upper House Speaker Abdi Hashi Abdullahi said relations between the two countries are built on friendship and mutual respect, recalling Erdoğan's 2011 visit.
items.imageAlt: The Turkish embassy in Mogadishu

items.title: Uganda begins withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly 20 years
items.summary: Uganda's army chief, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, said the withdrawal of UPDF troops from Somalia has begun and that security is being handed over to Somali forces. Garowe Online said the move comes as funding for support to the AUSSOM mission has been cut.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan troops serving with the African Union mission in Somalia mount a guard of honour (file photo, 2021)

items.title: Heritage Institute publishes a study on the role of civil society in Somalia
items.summary: The Heritage Institute for Policy Studies has released a study assessing the role, effectiveness and challenges of civil society organisations in Somalia, particularly their contribution to transparency and government accountability. The institute's director, Mursal Maxamuud Saney, said these organisations have played…
items.imageAlt: Members of civil society groups at a town hall meeting in Mogadishu (file photo, 2014)

items.title: Gen. Mohamed Ali Barise formally takes command of the Somali National Army
items.summary: It was reported that Gen. Barise, who was appointed on 25 October, took over from Gen. Madey Nuuray Sheikh Ufurow. Barise previously held the post from 2019 to 2020.
items.imageAlt: Somali National Army soldiers taking part in a military parade (2013)

items.title: Petroleum Authority: Curad-1 offshore oil well has reached a key layer
items.summary: The chairman of the Somali Petroleum Authority said drilling of the Curad-1 well, led by Turkish company TPAO, has reached a layer where signs of oil could appear. He said the final target is expected to be reached in December.
items.imageAlt: Turkish drilling ship Kanuni (2020), not the Çağrı Bey

items.title: Somaliland bans its residents from taking part in Somali politics
items.summary: Somaliland's Ministry of Interior issued an order saying that anyone who takes part in Somalia's political activities may face legal action. The order did not specify which activities it covers or how it will be enforced.
items.imageAlt: The House of Representatives building in Hargeisa (file photo, 2015)

items.title: UN mission ends without a mechanism to resolve the election dispute
items.summary: The United Nations political mission ends on Saturday without agreement on an alternative mechanism to mediate the dispute over the president's term of office. President Hassan Sheikh has invited the opposition to talks on 14–18 November, but the main opposition groups have not yet confirmed their participation.
items.imageAlt: A UN Security Council meeting on the situation in Somalia (file photo, 2019)

items.title: Hirshabelle approves a $47.45 million budget for 2027
items.summary: It was reported that Hirshabelle's council of ministers, chaired by President Gudlawe, approved the 2027 budget, which is 7% larger than the 2026 budget. The meeting also discussed security, elections and flood preparedness.
items.imageAlt: Map of Somalia showing Hirshabelle state

items.title: House of the People suspends sessions for two weeks to install the E-Parliament system
items.summary: Speaker of the House of the People Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur said sessions will be suspended from 31 October. He said the new system will introduce electronic voting and digital registration.
items.imageAlt: Federal MPs seated at a parliamentary ceremony (2016)

items.title: Somalia prepares for El Niño floods feared to worsen food shortages
items.summary: The World Food Programme (WFP) and partner agencies are strengthening emergency plans, including early warning, transport routes and cash assistance, ahead of the El Niño rains. Riverside communities were described as the most at risk.
items.imageAlt: Satellite image showing flooding along the Shabelle River

items.title: EU: Somali goods can enter its markets duty-free
items.summary: The EU delegation to Somalia said Somalia is one of 33 African countries that the 'Everything But Arms' scheme allows to export goods, except arms, to Europe duty-free. It was reported that the benefit depends on traders meeting European quality standards.
items.imageAlt: The port of Berbera, an export hub (2023)

items.title: Turkey says it will send a research and fishing vessel to Somalia's coast
items.summary: Turkish Ambassador to Somalia Ferhat Alkan announced, during National Fisheries Week in Mogadishu, that a research and fishing vessel will be sent to strengthen the skills of Somali fishermen. The vessel's name and arrival date have not been disclosed.
items.imageAlt: Fishing boats and nets on the shore at Garacad

items.title: Ethiopia says it has received 12 fighter jets from Russia
items.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced that Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 aircraft and is awaiting S-400 air defence systems, amid tension on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border.
items.imageAlt: A Su-35 fighter jet

items.title: Energy minister blames rising Mogadishu electricity prices on fuel costs
items.summary: Minister Abdullahi Bidhaan said the increase in electricity prices in Mogadishu resulted from fuel price inflation linked to tension in the Middle East, noting that the government had blocked a proposal to double prices.
items.imageAlt: An electricity pole in Mogadishu (file photo, 2015)

items.title: Farmaajo calls for an independent investigation into the Jamea fighting
items.summary: Former President Farmaajo accused the government of using the armed forces in political disputes. The government said 75 Al-Shabaab fighters were killed in the fighting.
items.imageAlt: Former President Farmaajo giving a speech (2017)

items.title: Somalia launches a five-year plan on youth, peace and security
items.summary: The 2026–2030 plan aims to increase the role of young people in peacebuilding.
items.imageAlt: Young people at a youth conference in Mogadishu (file photo, 2016)

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh postpones a planned trip to Russia
items.summary: Somalia's president has postponed the planned trip to Russia. The report linked the decision to Al-Shabaab attacks and election tensions.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud at a meeting (2015)

items.title: Residents take the weapons that were on a bombed vehicle on the outskirts of Buurhakabo
items.imageAlt: Soldiers silhouetted near Buurhakabo at dusk (file photo, 2013)

items.title: African Union forces prepare to withdraw from key bases
items.summary: The troop withdrawal has raised concern about the security situation in Somalia.
items.imageAlt: African Union troops waiting for an aircraft at Mogadishu airport (2011)

items.title: Museveni urges Somalis to unite to defeat Al-Shabaab
items.summary: The President of Uganda said unity is the key to overcoming the biggest challenge facing Somalia.
items.imageAlt: President Museveni welcoming President Hassan Sheikh at the Kampala summit (2023)

items.title: UN political mission in Somalia comes to an end
items.summary: The closure of the mission ends more than thirty years of UN support for peacebuilding and governance.
items.imageAlt: Nicholas Kay, UNSOM's first head, arrives in Mogadishu as the mission begins (2013)

items.title: Villa Somalia formally invites the Opposition Forum to consultations
items.summary: The Opposition Forum, which includes Deni and Ahmed Madobe, and the Nabad iyo Nolol party have been invited to the consultations, which will take place on 14–18 November.
items.imageAlt: Five members of the Madasha forum in a group photo
